| <a id="h273"></a>H273 | Tell the owner where an effective value actually came from | update | Echivalent | Reevaluat | Built in #1207, then fixed after eight adversarial reviews. The first found the stdlib parser was python-dotenv's pre-1.2.3 grammar, while the lock pins 1.2.3: the doctor could print value material as key names, a named-pipe .env was no longer loaded, and a data home named in the repo .env was no longer followed. The second found that the doctor sent the admin credential to whatever answered at the hub address, that more keys than serve.py's four were read before any .env was loaded, and that a one-case line of value material could still be printed as a name. The third found that the start itself read 31 more names before the load (so ten .env knobs, the audit key and the public-profile gate among them, were shown as in effect and were not), that two read-again entries were false, and that the MCP transport ignored a user token kept in .env. The fourth found that the MCP transport and the HTTP user guard asked different questions, so a lapsed or revoked user credential locked every route but left MCP open to a local caller; that the coordinator built its Orchestrator before the load, so its audit rows went unkeyed beside the hub's keyed ones; that an IPv6 bind (JARVIS_HOST=::1) escaped both loopback checks; and that the CLI sent the admin token to any hub. The fifth found that the admin tier still trusted a loopback caller once no admin credential was active, so after the owner revoked every credential a local process with no token could mint a fresh user token over HTTP and reopen the user routes and MCP (older than H273, but it falsified this row's credential sentence); that a managed user token that had expired counted as never configured; that the CLI asked the owner to set an admin token it had withheld; and that the supervisor wrote its respawns apart from a run-log named in .env. The sixth found that the sentence about minting did not hold where no admin credential was ever configured, that the offline recovery wrote a tokens.db the hub never read when the data home was named only in a .env (and a packaged build had none to run), that the CLI's withheld message fired on refusals https would not fix, and that a named-pipe .env still split the run-log. The seventh found that the supervisor now told its child a default the hub never read (a named-pipe .env hid the runtime from the brief), that the packaged recovery revived env tokens that had been rotated away or revoked, and that the CLI still asked for a token that was set. The eighth found that the packaged recovery still missed a token in the start environment or a moved data home, and left a LAN-bound app unable to start, and that the new hint called a valid user token refused on an admin verb and proposed a rotate that revoked the owner's working admin token. Every effective configuration key now carries the layer that supplied it, the note says when a .env value is not in effect, and every surface the row names reports names and layers only. The table. load_layered_env (agents/core/env_provenance.py:365) loads the files. Precedence: the process environment (the shell, a systemd EnvironmentFile, docker -e), then the repo .env, then the data-home .env, and the first layer to set a key wins (override=False). It keeps python-dotenv's behaviour: - Each file is read once, whether a regular file or a named pipe, the way python-dotenv reads it. 1Password mounts a .env as a FIFO. - The load is python-dotenv's public load_dotenv on the text that was read. The names come from python-dotenv's own parser (dotenv.parser.parse_stream), which logs nothing, so a bad line is warned about once. No private python-dotenv API is used. - PYTHON_DOTENV_DISABLED is checked before each layer, as python-dotenv checks it on every call, so a repo .env that sets it stops the data-home layer. Its spellings are python-dotenv's own, kept in env_config.py, the repo's one home for env-flag parsing (agents/core/env_config.py:112); a parity test pins them against python-dotenv's own switch. - The data home is a callable resolved after the repo layer is loaded, so a JARVIS_USER_HOME set in the repo .env names it, as before. A first-run home is scaffolded before its .env is read. - A second load in one process keeps a file's attribution only while the environment still holds the value that load set (a private digest, never the value), and works out afresh what the files shadow. The same file as both layers is read once. - It records which layer supplied each key, by diffing the environment around each file, and the lower layers that also define it (shadowed: their value is ignored). That answers "why is my .env change not applied?". - files() records what the load did with each file: its kind (file, fifo, absent, the same file as the repo .env, or disabled), whether it is present, and whether it was read. provenance() (agents/core/env_provenance.py:541) is the queryable in-process table; a key that appeared after the load reads as set while running. The hub loads first. load_hub_env (agents/core/env_provenance.py:463) is the hub's own load, once per process, so a named pipe is read once: - serve.py calls it before it builds the server and runs its guards (serve.py:244). The server's host, port, log level and shutdown timeout, the posture guards and the bind guard see a .env value, so a token in .env satisfies the bind guard. - The lifespan calls it before its boot guards (agents/web.py:473). The data home, logging, the orchestrator with its audit log, memory and budget ledger, and the router's detect() all read after it: the audit key, the public-profile seed gate, turn embeddings, the budget, the router's URLs and cloud keys in a .env are in effect. The boot guards, the front door among them, judge the loaded environment, so the late re-check was removed. - The coordinator (the systemd jarvis-runtime unit, compose runtime-coordinator) calls it first in run(), before its run-log path and cycle (scripts/coordinator.py:106), and again, idempotently, before it builds its Orchestrator (scripts/coordinator.py:73): it shares the hub's data root, so it keys the audit chain the hub keys. The supervisor that spawns it (scripts/runtime_supervisor.py) does not load, since its child would then read every file key as the process environment's; it reads the run-log path through hub_value (agents/core/env_provenance.py:490), the value the files give without loading them, and it hands its child only a path it found (the process, or a regular .env), which the child's load does not override, so both write that one run-log (scripts/runtime_supervisor.py:72; review-H273g m4). A path in a named-pipe .env, which the supervisor never reads, is not handed down: the child reads the pipe as the hub does, so the cycles land where the brief reads them, and only the supervisor's own events stay in the default file (_child_env, scripts/runtime_supervisor.py:110; review-H273h m1). An empty value is unset on both ends. The reality-evidence harness does too (agents/core/observability/reality_evidence.py:183). - agents/run.py, the REPL, loads before its logging and its imports (agents/run.py:21), so a log file or scanner pattern in .env is in effect. - PluginManager.build asks for it too (agents/core/plugin_manager.py:83), for any other entry. scripts/install_smoke.py does not load before it builds its isolated hub (a temp data root, from the process environment); its PluginManager.build loads afterwards, as for any entry. - Log redaction is imported first, so its switch stays the boot environment's alone: a .env cannot turn it off. Keys read before the load. note_for (agents/core/env_provenance.py:526) flags what is still read before any file can be. That is what importing agents.web freezes or resolves: the ASGI root path, the rate limit, CORS, CSP, the router's auto-deep switch, the analytics cap, the graph's Neo4j defaults, the app and data roots, and the log-redaction switch (agents/core/env_provenance.py:60). A .env value for them is recorded but not in effect, and the note says to set it in the process environment. - What locates the hub's own files (JARVIS_APP_ROOT, JARVIS_HOME, JARVIS_MEMORY_DIR) is never taken from a file (agents/core/env_provenance.py:69). A .env value would have split the stores between two roots. It is recorded and kept out of the environment, and its own note says so (agents/core/env_provenance.py:100). - JARVIS_USER_HOME from the repo .env names the data home and its .env. When JARVIS_HOME is not set, the stores opened while the hub was imported stay under the default root, and its note says so (agents/core/env_provenance.py:72). - Read again after the load, so a .env value is in effect (agents/core/env_provenance.py:93): DEV_MODE; the admin and user tokens (every guard reads them per request, the MCP transport included); the OAuth client ids; the trusted proxies. The lists are measured, not declared: - A test spies on the environment in a subprocess across the import and the whole start up to the load, with the data root set either way. Every Nerva name read there must be listed, and every listed name must be read there. - A second spy runs the start and a few requests. Every read-again name must be read after the load, and no name listed as read before the load may be (tests/test_h273d_provenance_review.py:667). The two false read-again entries are fixed: - The MCP transport, the HTTP user guard and the MCP identity check ask one predicate, _user_credential_required (agents/web.py:293; agents/core/routers/mcp.py:419). A token from .env guards MCP on this machine and lets a remote client in. The question is whether a credential was ever configured (_ever_configured, agents/web.py:109): an env token, active or superseded; a rotation or a revoke with --revoke-env, which leave the store's persistent flag; an issued token, live or expired. Such a credential that has lapsed, been rotated away or been revoked locks MCP exactly as it locks HTTP. The admin guard asks the same question for its tier (_admin_configured, agents/web.py:137), and so does the owner flag on /chat, so where an admin credential was ever configured and every credential is revoked or has expired, no local process mints its way back in over HTTP. Recovery is scripts/token_recover.py rotate admin on the box, which loads the hub's .env files first so it writes the tokens.db the hub reads, and says which (review-H273g m2); a packaged build first removes every JARVIS_ADMIN_TOKEN and JARVIS_USER_TOKEN from both places the app reads them, the data home's .env (wherever the home is) and the environment the app starts from, unsets JARVIS_HOST for the restart (the boot guard refuses a LAN bind with no token), then removes security/tokens.db under its data root (JARVIS_HOME and JARVIS_MEMORY_DIR named), because that file is also what records the rotations and revokes that superseded env tokens (docs/PACKAGING.md; review-H273h m2, review-H273i m1). The check lists the token table once per store: once a tier shows configured it stays so for that store (review-H273g n1). Only a hub that never had a credential of the tier trusts a localhost caller without one (for the exception, see Known limits). - The OAuth routes use the plugin manager's copy of the OAuth module (agents/core/routers/oauth.py:33), which re-reads the client ids after the load. Key names come from python-dotenv itself whenever it can be imported (text_keys, agents/core/env_provenance.py:202): every binding in file order, a rebound key each time. The stdlib port (_port_keys, agents/core/env_provenance.py:143) is 1.2.3's grammar and is the fallback for a broken install. A parity test pins it on 25 edge cases, including the BOM, escaped backslashes and a key rebound without "=". A seeded differential fuzz of 4,000 random files pins it too. derive (agents/core/env_provenance.py:327) builds the same table offline. It follows a data home named in the repo .env, or built from ${VAR}, resolving every binding in file order as load_dotenv does: the environment wins over the file's earlier values, a rebound key takes its last value, and a last binding without "=" sets nothing (agents/core/env_provenance.py:294). It parses each file once, keyed on its size, times and inode, and never opens a named pipe. Surfaces: - GET /api/admin/env/sources (agents/core/routers/admin.py:564) is admin-guarded and no-store, at the same boundary as GET /api/admin/env. Each key comes with its layer, a label, the layers it overrides, whether /api/admin/env masks its value, and its note. It also names what the load did with each file (path, kind, present, read); values are never included. - \`nerva doctor\`'s advisory config_sources check (scripts/doctor.py:702): - Reading the hub. It reads the running hub's own table when /readyz is ok, asking without a credential first. Every request to the hub goes over http or https, has a timeout, refuses a redirect, and never goes through a proxy to a hub on this machine (scripts/doctor.py:379). The hub address brackets an IPv6 bind (JARVIS_HOST=::1 gives http://\[::1\]:8080; scripts/doctor.py:297), and an unbracketed IPv6 address, whatever its first group (0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1 too), is read the way http.client dials it (scripts/doctor.py:337). The admin credential goes only to a hub on this machine, decided by its address rather than its spelling (127.0.0.2, 127.1, localhost., ::1 and ::ffff:127.0.0.1 count; scripts/doctor.py:353). config_sources sends it only after a refusal, and runtime_resolves only when no user token is set (scripts/doctor.py:395). Otherwise the doctor predicts the table from its own shell and says which of the two it did and why. - Which keys. It shows every key a .env file sets, and the shell's keys that the hub's code reads or that carry Nerva's prefixes. The hub's reads are found by reading agents/ and serve.py: helper calls, a bound mapping, \*_ENV constants (private ones too), a pool's from_env names and a descriptor's \*_env keyword (scripts/doctor.py:570). - Which names are printed. A .env name is printed when the hub reads it, .env.example declares it, it is an identifier with Nerva's prefix, or it is a plain one-case name with a value, an empty placeholder included (scripts/doctor.py:816). Any other name is counted, never printed (withheld_env_names). That includes a name shaped like a digest, a seed or an access key id, whatever follows its "=" (scripts/doctor.py:588); a value that is only = padding; a PEM line; a mixed-case name; and a name with control characters. - Hub mode. On this machine it reads the files the hub names to tell names from value material. For a hub on another machine it shows only the names Nerva knows, and says why. - Other reports. It names a .env that is not UTF-8, which the hub's load fails on (env_not_utf8), and a named pipe it does not open. For each key it prints the .env values a higher layer overrides and the note. Any failure inside the check becomes a named reason, never a crash. - The \`nerva\` CLI's client (agents/cli/client.py:116) follows the same transport rules: no redirect (urllib carried both tokens to wherever one pointed), no proxy to a hub on this machine, and http or https only. Its loopback rule is the doctor's, pinned equal over one table of spellings. It sends the admin token only to a hub on this machine or over https (agents/cli/client.py:156), never in clear text to another host, whether or not a user token is set; the user token goes to the hub it names. When it withheld the admin token and the hub refuses, it names that as one possible cause beside the user token, never as the only one (review-H273g m3). The hint reads the hub's own reason for the tier it wanted: a verb that needs the admin tier asks for JARVIS_ADMIN_TOKEN when only the user token is set, only a token of the wanted tier that was sent is named as refused, a hub with no token of the tier configured is named as such, and the recovery offered is the additive token_recover.py issue (rotate only for a leaked token, since it revokes every token of the tier; review-H273i m2); nerva status reads the same reason on its runnable and e-stop lines (_auth_hint, agents/cli/nerva.py:785; review-H273h m3, review-H273i m2, n4). - The settings plane: every row says default, set, undeclared, or unreadable (an encrypted secret whose key is lost) (value_source, agents/core/settings_db.py:699). A value a selected product posture puts in effect is named beside the stored one (in_effect, overlay). An unknown stored posture is off, and the posture is read in the listing's own connection; a stored row that is not JSON (the posture included) no longer reads as off: the whole store is validated when it is first opened and before every full listing (_require_readable_store, agents/core/settings_db.py:553), and the listing raises SettingsUnreadable instead (tests/test_h273d_provenance_review.py:739). \`nerva config list\` prints both (agents/cli/nerva.py:956). - The HUD's Admin "API keys & secrets" list shows each key's layer, the layers it overrides and its note (hydrateAdminKeys, frontend/src/api/live.ts:205; frontend/src/modes3.tsx:261). Hermes records provenance only for vault-supplied names, and its own notes ask for this per-key table; Nerva has it. Nerva has no managed or secret-source layer in the environment: vault secrets are injected at action time, not loaded into the environment. Known limits: - On Windows, key names are compared case-sensitively although the environment is not; that case is theoretical and not handled. - A raw uvicorn start binds where uvicorn's own flags say. JARVIS_HOST there, from a file or from the shell alike, reaches the Host-header guard and the boot guard's bind check, which judges that value rather than the address uvicorn bound. - In a process that loads more than once (tests), a value equal to one an earlier load set keeps that load's attribution. The hub loads once. - JARVIS_USER_HOME set only in a .env, with no JARVIS_HOME, still splits the stores: what the hub opens while it is imported stays under the default root, and the rest follows the home (autonomy.db opens under both). Its note says so on the route, in the doctor and in the HUD. Moving either half would move an existing install's history, so it is left, and set in the process environment it does not split. - The CLI sends the admin token to a hub on another machine when that hub is reached over https: the owner named that hub, and its admin verbs need it. The doctor, which only reads, never sends the admin token off this machine. Over plain http to another machine the admin verbs (the e-stop, approvals, tools, jobs) are refused, and the CLI says why. - A box that never had an admin credential trusts a direct localhost caller as admin, whatever happened to its user tokens: after revoke user --revoke-env, or once a user token has lapsed, a local process still mints a user token. The user-token lock binds callers from other machines; revoke all --revoke-env closes it for this one too (pinned, review-H273g m1). - A run-log path set only in a named-pipe .env reaches the coordinator and the hub, not the supervisor, which cannot read the pipe: its own spawned, child_exited and respawned events go to the default logs/runtime.jsonl, apart from the cycles. Setting the path in the process environment keeps them together. - A token issued with token_store issue and deleted by a revoke without --revoke-env leaves no trace in the store, and so does anything that empties it (purge_expired, which nothing in the hub calls, a deleted tokens.db, a new data root), so that hub reads as never configured for its tier at its next start and trusts a localhost caller again (a running hub that saw the credential stays locked until then). Closing it needs a persistent flag in agents/core/security/token_store.py, the owner's security lane. A rotation, a revoke with --revoke-env, or an expired token keep the hub locked. - A managed user token alone now guards this machine too (ENV-163): an install that has only a store token needs it in the HUD ("store in this browser"), the CLI, the doctor and nerva_mcp_stdio.py. - Under a raw uvicorn start, uvicorn's own proxy knobs (FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS, UVICORN_PROXY_HEADERS) are read before the app is imported, so a .env value for them is not in effect, while announce_trusted_proxies reports the file's value. - A trailing-dot name (localhost., 127.1.) counts as this machine, though the resolver treats it as a DNS name; a resolver that answered it with another address would receive the admin token. - The value-material shape misses uppercase hex, digitless base32 and short mixed ids, and withholds digit-bearing names with no underscore (contrived lines). - The data home is scaffolded (its README, a .env copied from .env.example) before the boot guards run, so a start they refuse still writes it. - Hub mode on this machine trusts the paths the hub names: a hub in a container names paths that do not exist on the host, and every plain custom key is then withheld with a reason that is false for it. - The scan for the hub's reads misses computed and mapped names (a URL key built from a prefix, a budget key read through a mapping); both are declared in .env.example or carry the prefix today. - JARVIS_HOST=0::0 or ::ffff:0.0.0.0 gives a URL judged not this machine (the proxy is used and the admin token withheld, the safe direction); JARVIS_HOST=localhost:9000 gives an invalid URL, as it did before. Tests: - tests/test_env_provenance.py (61 cases): parity and fuzz (tests/test_env_provenance.py:130), the named pipe, the plugin manager's order and the posture overlay. - tests/test_doctor_hub_credential.py (8): a real redirect and a real proxy, pinning where the credential goes (tests/test_doctor_hub_credential.py:93). - tests/test_h273c_provenance_review.py (56): the import, the names withheld, the bound-mapping scan and the second round's nits. - tests/test_h273d_provenance_review.py (74 cases, the third round): - the start measured and the lists by where they are used (tests/test_h273d_provenance_review.py:119); - knobs the start reads, in effect from a .env (tests/test_h273d_provenance_review.py:159); - the bind guard through serve.py and the lifespan, the redaction floor, one load per process, the refused roots; - the MCP transport, the OAuth routes, and the doctor's and CLI's transport rules; - hub mode, the names withheld, the widened scan, the reviewer's survivors and the nits. - tests/test_h273e_provenance_review.py (48 cases, the fourth round): the MCP transport, its per-tool identity check and the HTTP guard in every credential posture, rotated, expired, revoked, a managed token only and never configured (tests/test_h273e_provenance_review.py:59); the coordinator keying the audit chain from .env; the IPv6 bind; the CLI's admin-token destination; the CLI and doctor loopback rules over one table (tests/test_h273e_provenance_review.py:238); the REPL's log file; and the refused roots' note. - tests/test_h273f_provenance_review.py (43 cases, the fifth round): an admin env token alone closing the loopback fallback; no local caller mints a token once every credential is revoked or has expired, in three postures, while a box that never had an admin credential still mints its first from loopback; the owner flag on /chat; the offline recovery; an expired managed user token keeping the hub locked, and the recorded residual; the CLI's admin token for an admin-only environment and over the whole table of spellings, and what it says when it withholds it; the supervisor's and the coordinator's run-log from .env; hub_value's layers; the reality-evidence harness's load; a bare IPv6 hub whose first group is not empty. - tests/test_h273g_provenance_review.py (18 cases, the sixth round): a user-only box still trusting this machine as admin, and the docstrings that say so; an issued-only admin token, live and expired, closing the loopback fallback; the configured scope remembered per store; nothing purging expired tokens; the recovery writing the store a .env names; the CLI's hint for the client that was refused, with and without an admin token, and on nerva status's two lines; one run-log for a named-pipe .env and for a path the child is told; an empty run-log value; hub_value's disabled and interpolated layers; the supervisor run as a script. - tests/test_h273h_provenance_review.py (14 cases, the seventh round): a named-pipe run-log path reaching the coordinator and the hub alike, through a real load of the pipe; a process path handed down as it is; nothing handed down when the app cannot import; the packaged recovery removing the env tokens before the file, and naming the JARVIS_HOME path; a refused token that is set named as refused for each tier and both; the status lines, loopback and LAN; scripts/token_recover.py run as documented, as a script; both spawn sites in the supervisor's main() carrying the run-log. - tests/test_h273i_provenance_review.py (12 cases, the eighth round): the hint for each tier the hub names (a user token on an admin verb, a refused admin token and its issue verb, the user tier, a hub with no token of the tier), the verb passing the hub's reason, the status lines naming a hub with no user token, the child keeping its parent's environment, the packaged recovery naming both places, the bind and JARVIS_MEMORY_DIR, the test manual's recovery rows, and the supervisor's docstring. - tests/test_doctor.py keeps the JSON contract, and frontend/src/test/env-sources.test.ts the HUD mapping and its note. Mutation: - The first round's 41 mutants and the second's 29 were each caught, as were the second review's twelve survivors. - The third review's own 67 independent mutants left 16 survivors, four of them equivalent. Each of the other twelve now has a test: the lists' classification, a mixed-case name, a missing value, the data home's values, the cache key, a commented declaration, a 403, a posture that is not JSON, a third load, and the same-file order. Re-run against the new tests, all twelve are caught. - This round's 46 mutants (44 Python, 2 HUD) were each run against their own suites: 45 are caught. The survivor drops the IPv4-mapped check in the loopback test. It is equivalent on the test interpreter, whose patched ipaddress already counts ::ffff:127.0.0.1 as loopback, and the check stays for the 3.12 releases before that fix. - The fourth review's 50 independent mutants left three survivors (the MCP gate's predicate and two CLI loopback spellings); each is caught now. This round's 20 mutants (the bracketed IPv6 address and the bare IPv6 host in both copies, the CLI's admin-token destination, the shared predicate in the guard, the MCP gate and the identity check, the coordinator's and the REPL's load, the refused roots' note, the CLI's spellings) were all caught, one after the identity-check case was added. The fifth review's 22 independent mutants left four real survivors (the CLI with an admin token and no user token, a localhost-prefix spelling for the admin token, the coordinator's run() load, the reality-evidence harness's load); each has a case now. This round's 15 mutants (the ever-configured rule for both tiers and each of its terms, the CLI's hint, the supervisor's read and hub_value's layers, the bare IPv6 order in both copies) were caught but one, the admin rule ignoring the env token, which is caught now that the case exists; one more is equivalent (hub_value's early process-environment return, which the repo layer's merge gives anyway). The sixth review's 30 independent mutants left nine real survivors (an issued-only admin token, the generic hint, two hub_value layer rules, the supervisor run as a script, an empty run-log value, and three bare-IPv6 spellings in the safe direction); the first six have cases now. This round's 13 mutants were all caught, one after its case was added (the e-stop status line). The seventh review's 22 independent mutants left three real survivors (the recovery's import path run as a script, and the supervisor's two spawn sites); each has a case now. This round's 12 mutants were all caught, one after the supervisor's two .env readers became one (its import path, now covered by the script-run case). The eighth review's 22 independent mutants left one real survivor (the child's environment dropped whole) and one unpinned hint verb; both have cases, and this round's 12 mutants over the hint and the child's environment are all caught. Image-recovery collateral review (2026-10-02): changes to shared CLI/image-turn or HUD local-panel disclosure are outside this row's claimed symbols. Complete base evidence pins and unchanged text anchors verified; existing capability/status preserved. Claim-specific source inspection is recorded in the bounded image source review. MCP transport audit collateral review (2026-10-09): the route adds only fixed-field authentication telemetry at the existing RPC gate. This row's admin/listing, validation or transport-auth behavior and remaining limitations are unchanged; its previously current mcp.py pin and explicit coordinates were reviewed. Independent #1233 review (historical scope): Built in #1207, then fixed after eight adversarial reviews. The first found the stdlib parser was python-dotenv's pre-1.2.3 grammar, while the lock pins 1.2.3: the doctor could print value material as key names, a named-pipe .env was no longer loaded, and a data home named in the repo .env was no longer followed. The second found that the doctor sent the admin credential to whatever answered at the hub address, that more keys than serve.py's four were read before any .env was loaded, and that a one-case line of value material could still be printed as a name. The third found that the start itself read 31 more names before the load (so ten .env knobs, the audit key and the public-profile gate among them, were shown as in effect and were not), that two read-again entries were false, and that the MCP transport ignored a user token kept in .env. The fourth found that the MCP transport and the HTTP user guard asked different questions, so a lapsed or revoked user credential locked every route but left MCP open to a local caller; that the coordinator built its Orchestrator before the load, so its audit rows went unkeyed beside the hub's keyed ones; that an IPv6 bind (JARVIS_HOST=::1) escaped both loopback checks; and that the CLI sent the admin token to any hub. The fifth found that the admin tier still trusted a loopback caller once no admin credential was active, so after the owner revoked every credential a local process with no token could mint a fresh user token over HTTP and reopen the user routes and MCP (older than H273, but it falsified this row's credential sentence); that a managed user token that had expired counted as never configured; that the CLI asked the owner to set an admin token it had withheld; and that the supervisor wrote its respawns apart from a run-log named in .env. The sixth found that the sentence about minting did not hold where no admin credential was ever configured, that the offline recovery wrote a tokens.db the hub never read when the data home was named only in a .env (and a packaged build had none to run), that the CLI's withheld message fired on refusals https would not fix, and that a named-pipe .env still split the run-log. The seventh found that the supervisor now told its child a default the hub never read (a named-pipe .env hid the runtime from the brief), that the packaged recovery revived env tokens that had been rotated away or revoked, and that the CLI still asked for a token that was set. The eighth found that the packaged recovery still missed a token in the start environment or a moved data home, and left a LAN-bound app unable to start, and that the new hint called a valid user token refused on an admin verb and proposed a rotate that revoked the owner's working admin token. Every effective configuration key now carries the layer that supplied it, the note says when a .env value is not in effect, and every surface the row names reports names and layers only. The table. load_layered_env (agents/core/env_provenance.py:365) loads the files. Precedence: the process environment (the shell, a systemd EnvironmentFile, docker -e), then the repo .env, then the data-home .env, and the first layer to set a key wins (override=False). It keeps python-dotenv's behaviour: - Each file is read once, whether a regular file or a named pipe, the way python-dotenv reads it. 1Password mounts a .env as a FIFO. - The load is python-dotenv's public load_dotenv on the text that was read. The names come from python-dotenv's own parser (dotenv.parser.parse_stream), which logs nothing, so a bad line is warned about once. No private python-dotenv API is used. - PYTHON_DOTENV_DISABLED is checked before each layer, as python-dotenv checks it on every call, so a repo .env that sets it stops the data-home layer. Its spellings are python-dotenv's own, kept in env_config.py, the repo's one home for env-flag parsing (agents/core/env_config.py:112); a parity test pins them against python-dotenv's own switch. - The data home is a callable resolved after the repo layer is loaded, so a JARVIS_USER_HOME set in the repo .env names it, as before. A first-run home is scaffolded before its .env is read. - A second load in one process keeps a file's attribution only while the environment still holds the value that load set (a private digest, never the value), and works out afresh what the files shadow. The same file as both layers is read once. - It records which layer supplied each key, by diffing the environment around each file, and the lower layers that also define it (shadowed: their value is ignored). That answers "why is my .env change not applied?". - files() records what the load did with each file: its kind (file, fifo, absent, the same file as the repo .env, or disabled), whether it is present, and whether it was read. provenance() (agents/core/env_provenance.py:541) is the queryable in-process table; a key that appeared after the load reads as set while running. The hub loads first. load_hub_env (agents/core/env_provenance.py:463) is the hub's own load, once per process, so a named pipe is read once: - serve.py calls it before it builds the server and runs its guards (serve.py:244). The server's host, port, log level and shutdown timeout, the posture guards and the bind guard see a .env value, so a token in .env satisfies the bind guard. - The lifespan calls it before its boot guards (agents/web.py:473). The data home, logging, the orchestrator with its audit log, memory and budget ledger, and the router's detect() all read after it: the audit key, the public-profile seed gate, turn embeddings, the budget, the router's URLs and cloud keys in a .env are in effect. The boot guards, the front door among them, judge the loaded environment, so the late re-check was removed. - The coordinator (the systemd jarvis-runtime unit, compose runtime-coordinator) calls it first in run(), before its run-log path and cycle (scripts/coordinator.py:106), and again, idempotently, before it builds its Orchestrator (scripts/coordinator.py:73): it shares the hub's data root, so it keys the audit chain the hub keys. The supervisor that spawns it (scripts/runtime_supervisor.py) does not load, since its child would then read every file key as the process environment's; it reads the run-log path through hub_value (agents/core/env_provenance.py:490), the value the files give without loading them, and it hands its child only a path it found (the process, or a regular .env), which the child's load does not override, so both write that one run-log (scripts/runtime_supervisor.py:72; review-H273g m4). A path in a named-pipe .env, which the supervisor never reads, is not handed down: the child reads the pipe as the hub does, so the cycles land where the brief reads them, and only the supervisor's own events stay in the default file (_child_env, scripts/runtime_supervisor.py:110; review-H273h m1). An empty value is unset on both ends. The reality-evidence harness does too (agents/core/observability/reality_evidence.py:183). - agents/run.py, the REPL, loads before its logging and its imports (agents/run.py:21), so a log file or scanner pattern in .env is in effect. - PluginManager.build asks for it too (agents/core/plugin_manager.py:83), for any other entry. scripts/install_smoke.py does not load before it builds its isolated hub (a temp data root, from the process environment); its PluginManager.build loads afterwards, as for any entry. - Log redaction is imported first, so its switch stays the boot environment's alone: a .env cannot turn it off. Keys read before the load. note_for (agents/core/env_provenance.py:526) flags what is still read before any file can be. That is what importing agents.web freezes or resolves: the ASGI root path, the rate limit, CORS, CSP, the router's auto-deep switch, the analytics cap, the graph's Neo4j defaults, the app and data roots, and the log-redaction switch (agents/core/env_provenance.py:60). A .env value for them is recorded but not in effect, and the note says to set it in the process environment. - What locates the hub's own files (JARVIS_APP_ROOT, JARVIS_HOME, JARVIS_MEMORY_DIR) is never taken from a file (agents/core/env_provenance.py:69). A .env value would have split the stores between two roots. It is recorded and kept out of the environment, and its own note says so (agents/core/env_provenance.py:100). - JARVIS_USER_HOME from the repo .env names the data home and its .env. When JARVIS_HOME is not set, the stores opened while the hub was imported stay under the default root, and its note says so (agents/core/env_provenance.py:72). - Read again after the load, so a .env value is in effect (agents/core/env_provenance.py:93): DEV_MODE; the admin and user tokens (every guard reads them per request, the MCP transport included); the OAuth client ids; the trusted proxies. The lists are measured, not declared: - A test spies on the environment in a subprocess across the import and the whole start up to the load, with the data root set either way. Every Nerva name read there must be listed, and every listed name must be read there. - A second spy runs the start and a few requests. Every read-again name must be read after the load, and no name listed as read before the load may be (tests/test_h273d_provenance_review.py:667). The two false read-again entries are fixed: - The MCP transport, the HTTP user guard and the MCP identity check ask one predicate, _user_credential_required (agents/web.py:293; agents/core/routers/mcp.py:419). A token from .env guards MCP on this machine and lets a remote client in. The question is whether a credential was ever configured (_ever_configured, agents/web.py:109): an env token, active or superseded; a rotation or a revoke with --revoke-env, which leave the store's persistent flag; an issued token, live or expired. Such a credential that has lapsed, been rotated away or been revoked locks MCP exactly as it locks HTTP. The admin guard asks the same question for its tier (_admin_configured, agents/web.py:137), and so does the owner flag on /chat, so where an admin credential was ever configured and every credential is revoked or has expired, no local process mints its way back in over HTTP. Recovery is scripts/token_recover.py rotate admin on the box, which loads the hub's .env files first so it writes the tokens.db the hub reads, and says which (review-H273g m2); a packaged build first removes every JARVIS_ADMIN_TOKEN and JARVIS_USER_TOKEN from both places the app reads them, the data home's .env (wherever the home is) and the environment the app starts from, unsets JARVIS_HOST for the restart (the boot guard refuses a LAN bind with no token), then removes security/tokens.db under its data root (JARVIS_HOME and JARVIS_MEMORY_DIR named), because that file is also what records the rotations and revokes that superseded env tokens (docs/PACKAGING.md; review-H273h m2, review-H273i m1). The check lists the token table once per store: once a tier shows configured it stays so for that store (review-H273g n1). Only a hub that never had a credential of the tier trusts a localhost caller without one (for the exception, see Known limits). - The OAuth routes use the plugin manager's copy of the OAuth module (agents/core/routers/oauth.py:35), which re-reads the client ids after the load. Key names come from python-dotenv itself whenever it can be imported (text_keys, agents/core/env_provenance.py:202): every binding in file order, a rebound key each time. The stdlib port (_port_keys, agents/core/env_provenance.py:143) is 1.2.3's grammar and is the fallback for a broken install. A parity test pins it on 25 edge cases, including the BOM, escaped backslashes and a key rebound without "=". A seeded differential fuzz of 4,000 random files pins it too. derive (agents/core/env_provenance.py:327) builds the same table offline. It follows a data home named in the repo .env, or built from ${VAR}, resolving every binding in file order as load_dotenv does: the environment wins over the file's earlier values, a rebound key takes its last value, and a last binding without "=" sets nothing (agents/core/env_provenance.py:294). It parses each file once, keyed on its size, times and inode, and never opens a named pipe. Surfaces: - GET /api/admin/env/sources (agents/core/routers/admin.py:564) is admin-guarded and no-store, at the same boundary as GET /api/admin/env. Each key comes with its layer, a label, the layers it overrides, whether /api/admin/env masks its value, and its note. It also names what the load did with each file (path, kind, present, read); values are never included. - \`nerva doctor\`'s advisory config_sources check (scripts/doctor.py:702): - Reading the hub. It reads the running hub's own table when /readyz is ok, asking without a credential first. Every request to the hub goes over http or https, has a timeout, refuses a redirect, and never goes through a proxy to a hub on this machine (scripts/doctor.py:379). The hub address brackets an IPv6 bind (JARVIS_HOST=::1 gives http://\[::1\]:8080; scripts/doctor.py:297), and an unbracketed IPv6 address, whatever its first group (0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1 too), is read the way http.client dials it (scripts/doctor.py:337). The admin credential goes only to a hub on this machine, decided by its address rather than its spelling (127.0.0.2, 127.1, localhost., ::1 and ::ffff:127.0.0.1 count; scripts/doctor.py:353). config_sources sends it only after a refusal, and runtime_resolves only when no user token is set (scripts/doctor.py:395). Otherwise the doctor predicts the table from its own shell and says which of the two it did and why. - Which keys. It shows every key a .env file sets, and the shell's keys that the hub's code reads or that carry Nerva's prefixes. The hub's reads are found by reading agents/ and serve.py: helper calls, a bound mapping, \*_ENV constants (private ones too), a pool's from_env names and a descriptor's \*_env keyword (scripts/doctor.py:570). - Which names are printed. A .env name is printed when the hub reads it, .env.example declares it, it is an identifier with Nerva's prefix, or it is a plain one-case name with a value, an empty placeholder included (scripts/doctor.py:816). Any other name is counted, never printed (withheld_env_names). That includes a name shaped like a digest, a seed or an access key id, whatever follows its "=" (scripts/doctor.py:588); a value that is only = padding; a PEM line; a mixed-case name; and a name with control characters. - Hub mode. On this machine it reads the files the hub names to tell names from value material. For a hub on another machine it shows only the names Nerva knows, and says why. - Other reports. It names a .env that is not UTF-8, which the hub's load fails on (env_not_utf8), and a named pipe it does not open. For each key it prints the .env values a higher layer overrides and the note. Any failure inside the check becomes a named reason, never a crash. - The \`nerva\` CLI's client (agents/cli/client.py:116) follows the same transport rules: no redirect (urllib carried both tokens to wherever one pointed), no proxy to a hub on this machine, and http or https only. Its loopback rule is the doctor's, pinned equal over one table of spellings. It sends the admin token only to a hub on this machine or over https (agents/cli/client.py:156), never in clear text to another host, whether or not a user token is set; the user token goes to the hub it names. When it withheld the admin token and the hub refuses, it names that as one possible cause beside the user token, never as the only one (review-H273g m3). The hint reads the hub's own reason for the tier it wanted: a verb that needs the admin tier asks for JARVIS_ADMIN_TOKEN when only the user token is set, only a token of the wanted tier that was sent is named as refused, a hub with no token of the tier configured is named as such, and the recovery offered is the additive token_recover.py issue (rotate only for a leaked token, since it revokes every token of the tier; review-H273i m2); nerva status reads the same reason on its runnable and e-stop lines (_auth_hint, agents/cli/nerva.py:795; review-H273h m3, review-H273i m2, n4). - The settings plane: every row says default, set, undeclared, or unreadable (an encrypted secret whose key is lost) (value_source, agents/core/settings_db.py:701). A value a selected product posture puts in effect is named beside the stored one (in_effect, overlay). An unknown stored posture is off, and the posture is read in the listing's own connection; a stored row that is not JSON (the posture included) no longer reads as off: the whole store is validated when it is first opened and before every full listing (_require_readable_store, agents/core/settings_db.py:553), and the listing raises SettingsUnreadable instead (tests/test_h273d_provenance_review.py:739). \`nerva config list\` prints both (agents/cli/nerva.py:966). - The HUD's Admin "API keys & secrets" list shows each key's layer, the layers it overrides and its note (hydrateAdminKeys, frontend/src/api/live.ts:205; frontend/src/modes3.tsx:261). Hermes records provenance only for vault-supplied names, and its own notes ask for this per-key table; Nerva has it. Nerva has no managed or secret-source layer in the environment: vault secrets are injected at action time, not loaded into the environment. Known limits: - On Windows, key names are compared case-sensitively although the environment is not; that case is theoretical and not handled. - A raw uvicorn start binds where uvicorn's own flags say. JARVIS_HOST there, from a file or from the shell alike, reaches the Host-header guard and the boot guard's bind check, which judges that value rather than the address uvicorn bound. - In a process that loads more than once (tests), a value equal to one an earlier load set keeps that load's attribution. The hub loads once. - JARVIS_USER_HOME set only in a .env, with no JARVIS_HOME, still splits the stores: what the hub opens while it is imported stays under the default root, and the rest follows the home (autonomy.db opens under both). Its note says so on the route, in the doctor and in the HUD. Moving either half would move an existing install's history, so it is left, and set in the process environment it does not split. - The CLI sends the admin token to a hub on another machine when that hub is reached over https: the owner named that hub, and its admin verbs need it. The doctor, which only reads, never sends the admin token off this machine. Over plain http to another machine the admin verbs (the e-stop, approvals, tools, jobs) are refused, and the CLI says why. - A box that never had an admin credential trusts a direct localhost caller as admin, whatever happened to its user tokens: after revoke user --revoke-env, or once a user token has lapsed, a local process still mints a user token. The user-token lock binds callers from other machines; revoke all --revoke-env closes it for this one too (pinned, review-H273g m1). - A run-log path set only in a named-pipe .env reaches the coordinator and the hub, not the supervisor, which cannot read the pipe: its own spawned, child_exited and respawned events go to the default logs/runtime.jsonl, apart from the cycles. Setting the path in the process environment keeps them together. - A token issued with token_store issue and deleted by a revoke without --revoke-env leaves no trace in the store, and so does anything that empties it (purge_expired, which nothing in the hub calls, a deleted tokens.db, a new data root), so that hub reads as never configured for its tier at its next start and trusts a localhost caller again (a running hub that saw the credential stays locked until then). Closing it needs a persistent flag in agents/core/security/token_store.py, the owner's security lane. A rotation, a revoke with --revoke-env, or an expired token keep the hub locked. - A managed user token alone now guards this machine too (ENV-163): an install that has only a store token needs it in the HUD ("store in this browser"), the CLI, the doctor and nerva_mcp_stdio.py. - Under a raw uvicorn start, uvicorn's own proxy knobs (FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS, UVICORN_PROXY_HEADERS) are read before the app is imported, so a .env value for them is not in effect, while announce_trusted_proxies reports the file's value. - A trailing-dot name (localhost., 127.1.) counts as this machine, though the resolver treats it as a DNS name; a resolver that answered it with another address would receive the admin token. - The value-material shape misses uppercase hex, digitless base32 and short mixed ids, and withholds digit-bearing names with no underscore (contrived lines). - The data home is scaffolded (its README, a .env copied from .env.example) before the boot guards run, so a start they refuse still writes it. - Hub mode on this machine trusts the paths the hub names: a hub in a container names paths that do not exist on the host, and every plain custom key is then withheld with a reason that is false for it. - The scan for the hub's reads misses computed and mapped names (a URL key built from a prefix, a budget key read through a mapping); both are declared in .env.example or carry the prefix today. - JARVIS_HOST=0::0 or ::ffff:0.0.0.0 gives a URL judged not this machine (the proxy is used and the admin token withheld, the safe direction); JARVIS_HOST=localhost:9000 gives an invalid URL, as it did before. | <a id="h275"></a>H275 | Boot into a known-good state when customizations break the install | copy | Echivalent | Reevaluat | The hub can boot in safe mode, with every owner customization left out and no gate relaxed. JARVIS_SAFE_MODE=1, or \`python serve.py --safe-mode\`, which sets it before the hub is imported (apply_safe_mode_switch, serve.py:18), is the one flag, read at call time by one module (enabled, agents/core/safe_mode.py:140). The runtime (scripts/runtime_supervisor.py, which passes it to scripts/coordinator.py) takes --safe-mode too, since it runs heartbeats, owner jobs and agents on the same data root; deploy/systemd/README.md says to set JARVIS_SAFE_MODE=1 in the env file both units read and restart both. It leaves out the owner's layers (15 since H490, H594, H613 and H464c, whose \`company_mode\` layer leaves the company-mode sweep out; LAYERS, agents/core/safe_mode.py:63). Skills: discovery does not open the data home's skills folder (agents/core/skills/loader.py:647), and any skill in the bundled tree that is not a shipped one (generated, imported, edited or pending review, by the loader's own external classification) is not loaded (agents/core/skills/loader.py:722); every shipped skill still is. Approving a pending skill in safe mode signs it but says it loads on the next normal boot (loaded: false; agents/core/routers/skills.py:753). MCP: the saved servers are not registered (agents/web.py:1958; mcp_servers is reported only for a non-empty saved list) and their saved configuration is not touched: _save_mcp_config never rewrites it from the empty manager (agents/web.py:1929), and adding or removing a server answers 409 \`safe_mode\` before anything changes (_safe_mode_refusal, agents/core/routers/mcp.py:174). Acquired packages and extensions: the acquisition runtime reports itself disabled (agents/core/acquisition/runtime.py:44), and names acquired packages as left out only when acquisition was switched on, so nothing promoted is re-registered and extensions() returns None, which the activate route answers as unavailable. Plugin grants: JARVIS_PLUGIN_GRANTS, which only ever widens access under least privilege, is ignored (agents/core/plugin_gate.py:670). Persona and contract overlays: soul_path_for (agents/core/agent.py:389) and identity_path (agents/core/agent.py:438) resolve through _pick_overlay (agents/core/agent.py:375), which in safe mode returns the shipped SOUL.md or IDENTITY.md and never a SOUL.local.md or IDENTITY.local.md from the data home or the repository; construction and the H672 compaction-boundary refresh both resolve through it, so a safe-mode session cannot pick an overlay up mid-conversation. Heartbeat: a HEARTBEAT.local.md is passed over for the shipped HEARTBEAT.md (agents/core/heartbeat.py:215-220). An overlay that cannot even be probed (an unreadable souls folder) counts as left out rather than stopping the boot (present, agents/core/safe_mode.py:157), for personas and heartbeats alike. Owner jobs stay saved and are not put on the scheduler, neither at boot (agents/core/scheduler_service.py:64) nor by a later create, /remind, edit, resume or first run: JobRunner._held (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:1420) keeps register and register_manual off the scheduler, and a queued request waits for a normal boot. A manual tick is refused, run now answers 409 safe_mode (agents/core/routers/jobs.py:356), and the create confirmation says the job fires after a normal boot. What was left out is recorded by layer (note, agents/core/safe_mode.py:145; status, agents/core/safe_mode.py:244), logged once per layer and at boot (agents/web.py:499), and said on /healthz as a boolean (agents/core/routers/ops.py:56), on /readyz, whose readiness is unaffected (agents/core/routers/ops.py:142), on /status (agents/core/routers/status.py:109) and /api/status (agents/core/routers/status.py:119). The HUD reads it from /status (frontend/src/api/loaders.ts) and shows a red SAFE MODE strip that names the layers left out and cannot be dismissed, and says to restart without --safe-mode or JARVIS_SAFE_MODE (SafeModeBanner, frontend/src/safe-mode-banner.tsx). Safe mode only removes capability: core kernel, security, secrets and approval authority is not relaxed. Optional advisory judging and video analysis refuse in safe mode, and a test pins the exact list of modules that name it. | <a id="h285"></a>H285 | Choose which skills, plugins and MCP servers load at startup | update | Echivalent | Reevaluat | The owner declares which skills, plugins and MCP servers load at boot, and a plugin toggle survives a restart. Six declared settings rows (agents/core/settings_db.py:447-452), category \`loadset\`, hold comma lists: skills_disabled/skills_only, plugins_disabled/plugins_only, mcp_disabled/mcp_only, editable from the settings page and \`nerva config set\` (which says a loadset.\* key or a plugin switch applies at the next start). A disabled name does not load; a non-empty only-list loads only what it names; the disabled list wins (permits, agents/core/load_set.py:96). A list is read at call time (declared, agents/core/load_set.py:74), trimmed, de-duplicated and bounded to 256 names of at most 128 characters without control characters (parse_names, agents/core/load_set.py:43), and an unreadable store narrows nothing. For plugins the settings page's existing per-plugin \`plugins.\<id\>\` switches, which nothing used to read, count too: an explicit off is off (agents/core/load_set.py:84). SkillLoader.discover reads the lists once per pass (agents/core/skills/loader.py:654-655) and a skill named by its registry name or its folder is not registered at all, before any quarantine row (agents/core/skills/loader.py:733); a registration from an earlier pass is taken out when a later pass denies it, the per-pass snapshot is cleared in a finally, and in safe mode (the owner folder unread) no declared name is reported as unknown. PermissionGate switches off the plugins the lists name when it is built (apply_load_set, agents/core/plugin_gate.py:704), and PluginManager.build drops them from orch.plugins before binding oracle_bridge and Argus (_drop_switched_off, agents/core/plugin_manager.py:198), so the probes, the dashboard and WorldView never reach a switched-off plugin. Each gate holds its own copies of the built-in manifests (agents/core/plugin_gate.py:698), so switching one off never reaches the module table or another gate, and the readers of a plugin's enabled state ask the live gate: CloudImageRuntime is wired with orch.permission_gate (_available, agents/core/cloud_image_runtime.py:542) and the capability board reads the gate's manifests (_plugin_records, agents/core/observability/capability_registry.py:127). The plugin toggle (toggle_plugin, agents/core/routers/plugins.py:99) keeps the choice in one place, the plugin's plugins.\<id\> settings switch when it has one and otherwise plugins_disabled; switched on, it leaves plugins_disabled and joins a declared plugins_only (persist_plugin, agents/core/load_set.py:140). It reads the lists fail-closed (read_setting), so an unreadable store is not overwritten, and answers \`persisted\` (false when the store refused or could not be read, the live toggle standing). It writes a SETTINGS_CHANGE audit row naming the keys, and a re-enable that cannot be audited is switched back off and answers 503 audit_failed. The MCP load registers only the permitted saved servers (agents/web.py:1967-1974); a switched-off one is held (_MCP_HELD, agents/web.py:1944) and written back unchanged by every save, so the saved configuration never loses it, and adding a server of that name or removing it answers 409 \`switched_off\` naming the list (_held_refusal, agents/core/routers/mcp.py:159). The lists only narrow: nothing is installed, approved, registered or written to the approval store, and a declared name that matches nothing installed is reported as unknown (finish, agents/core/load_set.py:121). The status rows carry it: /skills (agents/core/routers/skills.py:76), /plugins (agents/core/routers/plugins.py:88) and /api/admin/mcp (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:132) return \`load_set\` with the declared lists, what was switched off and what is unknown (status, agents/core/load_set.py:132). | <a id="h288"></a>H288 | Scheduled and queued work, and its delivery destination | update | Parțial | Reevaluat | Three cron-lane clauses of Hermes' contract are unmet. The Kanban claim-lease and crash-grace asks are done. 1. HERMES_CRON_TIMEOUT: the plain cron path has no per-run wall clock. \`JobRunner._fire_once\` → \`_execute\` → \`_ask\`/\`_brief\`/\`_deliver\` (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:1735-1804, 1846-1872, 1874-1968, 2052-2080) has no \`asyncio.wait_for\` at any level. In particular, \`_send_tracked\`/\`_send\` (jobs.py:2082-2115) awaits the channel adapter bare. A hung Telegram/Discord send therefore holds the job's gate stripe (jobs_dispatch.py:44-59) and its APScheduler \`max_instances=1\` slot, and nothing breaks it. The script path already does this correctly: \`asyncio.wait_for(self.runner._ask(...), 120)\` at agents/core/autonomy/jobs_scripts.py:461 and \`asyncio.wait_for(self.runner._send_tracked(...), 30)\` at :513. The fix is to apply the same bound to the cron path, ideally as a \`jobs.run_timeout_seconds\` setting next to the existing \`jobs.media_send_timeout_seconds\`. The overrun should be recorded as a normal failed run through \`_failed\`, so the 3-strike pause and the incident path still apply. 2. \`JARVIS_TASK_MAX_SECONDS\` defaults to 0, which means unbounded (agents/core/autonomy/executor.py:57-60, agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:2014-2018). Out of the box, a hung in-process queued task is bounded only by the 3600 s stuck-running reaper. Fix: give it a non-zero shipped default, or promote it to a validated \`autonomy.\*\` setting like \`running_ttl_seconds\`, and add a test asserting the default is finite. 3. HERMES_CRON_SESSION_DB_TIMEOUT: the jobs store opens sqlite with neither \`timeout=\` nor \`PRAGMA busy_timeout\` (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:767-770). The task queue sets \`timeout=30.0\` + \`PRAGMA busy_timeout=30000\` (agents/core/autonomy/queue.py:402-404). jobs.db writers therefore fall back to SQLite's 5 s default, on a WAL shared by the gateway drain loop and cron firings. One-line parity fix. Out of scope, not gaps: the row's own rationale excludes the delivery-destination knobs (_AUTO_DELIVER_PLATFORM / _CHAT_ID / _THREAD_ID, TELEGRAM_CRON_THREAD_ID). The residual ~14-knob multi-agent Kanban board (_BOARD / _WORKSPACES_ROOT / _ATTACHMENTS_ROOT / _GOAL_MODE / _DISPATCH_IN_GATEWAY) is a product decision about whether Nerva grows a shared task board, not a slice of this row. | <a id="h313"></a>H313 | Speak | update | Echivalent | Reevaluat | The model can decide to say one short text aloud on one room's device, and can do it again. register_speak_tool (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:684) adds a ToolRPC \`speak\` tool with gated=True, trusted execution and its own gated intake (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:711, agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:717). It is registered only while JARVIS_MEDIA_DIRECTOR is on (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:697), and AutonomyCoordinator wires it with the broker kernel and the governed enqueue (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:922, agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:2201). It reaches the same Media Director instance the media routes use, so the owner's device registry and session board apply (agents/core/routers/media_director.py:272). SpeakTool.preflight (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:388) runs at proposal and again before the approved run. It refuses text over the spoken-reply cap and code-only text (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:394, agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:396). It resolves a room to that room's one announce-capable default device, so the card title and the persisted args name the speaker (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:268, agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:467). It raises no card the run could only refuse: unified API off, kernel off or unbound, no media root, no speech backend, no driver for the device, or no configured presence room each refuse by name (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:415, agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:410). SpeakTool.intake (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:445) shows the kernel the exact toolrpc.speak row it enqueues. Under the production composition (worker.kernel_gate over MediationKernelBridge, agents/core/autonomy/worker.py:681, agents/core/kernel/binding.py:132) that decision binds as the row's intake evidence, and a DENY raises no card (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:471). Only the human-accepted durable toolrpc.speak row runs. The kind is trusted (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:69) and the executor routes it to the trusted rail (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:2222-2225). ToolRPC re-runs the preflight and requires the trusted execution context (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:678, agents/core/tool_rpc.py:706), and the handler refuses a row of any other kind (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:541). SpeakTool.execute (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:536) synthesizes the clip through SpokenReply on the host TTSEngine in the owner's configured voice (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:552, agents/core/channels/spoken_reply.py:265, agents/core/voice/tts.py:216). It writes the clip owner-only under the first media root (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:639, agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:653) and presents it only through CapabilityActionAPI.perform('action:media.present') in announce mode (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:592, agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:597). The facade asks the Action Kernel before the handler runs (agents/core/capability_actions.py:176) and refuses on a DENY (agents/core/capability_actions.py:183), so the kernel authorizes the effect and the tool never reaches a driver. A kernel QUEUE on that present is honoured as the accepted row and audited as speak.durably_approved (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:500, agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:522). A DENY becomes kernel_denied with the kernel's reason (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:614). The Media Director treats an announce as a one-shot notice (agents/core/media_director.py:738): it never blocks the next present and costs no interrupt budget (agents/core/media_director.py:890), and whatever it cut into stays the restore point (agents/core/media_director.py:992). Because the tool is gated, tool_profiles offers it only to the owner on the operator surface (agents/core/tool_profiles.py:190, agents/core/tool_profiles.py:194), and the snapshot pins this (tests/_snapshots/tool_profiles.json:64, tests/test_tool_profiles.py:202). Tests cover: registration and postures (tests/test_speak_tool.py:170, tests/test_speak_tool.py:196); named preflight refusals that enqueue nothing (tests/test_speak_tool.py:271, tests/test_speak_tool.py:320); and the card naming the device (tests/test_speak_tool.py:286). With the real kernel.authorize, AutonomyPolicy and KillSwitch behind worker.kernel_gate, an approved speak is mediated and audited, and an engaged kill switch refuses both the run and the card (tests/test_speak_tool.py:520, tests/test_speak_tool.py:543, tests/test_speak_tool.py:576). Three back-to-back normal speaks on one device all play at no budget cost (tests/test_speak_tool.py:591). Speaking over music needs high urgency, pays once and keeps the music as the restore point (tests/test_speak_tool.py:608, tests/test_media_director.py:762). A kernel DENY, a missing TTS backend, a missing media root and a driverless device each refuse by name with no playback, and an engine that yields no audio refuses as tts_failed with nothing presented (tests/test_speak_tool.py:681, tests/test_speak_tool.py:469, tests/test_speak_tool.py:666, tests/test_speak_tool.py:703, tests/test_speak_tool.py:716). A row of another kind cannot speak (tests/test_speak_tool.py:753), and the clip spool stays bounded (tests/test_speak_tool.py:779). Known limits outside the accepted adaptation: an accepted speak runs at the next autonomy tick (default 60 s, floor 15 s, agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:566), like every gated tool. A presence:auto card names the sentinel, because only play time knows whether the owner is in the presence room. Audible output needs an owner-wired speaker driver (the in-repo NullMediaDriver refuses and LocalFileMediaDriver is a reference), the same host seam as every media.present. The speech-backend gate (tts_installed, agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:191) needs edge-tts, Kokoro, Piper with a model or the approved TTS command, with edge-tts and the command left out under voice.local_only, like the spoken-reply channel; a named TTS provider alone does not pass it. An announce of any length, including one sent through POST /api/media/present, no longer holds its device, as docs/FLAGS.md states. Hermes's tts.provider, custom command providers and tts.speed are outside the accepted adaptation, because Nerva's TTS subsystem was already ahead. | <a id="h314"></a>H314 | Let the model decide what to remember | update | Echivalent | Reevaluat | The model now writes its own long-term memory during a turn, through a tool that is atomic, guarded, recorded and undoable. \`memory\` (register_memory_tool, agents/core/memory_tool.py:413; registered ungated at agents/core/memory_tool.py:519 and wired from the autonomy coordinator's H314 block, whose \`_living_memory\` getter and \`register_memory_tool(\` call tests/test_h314_memory_tool.py:544-546 reads back from the coordinator's source) takes \`operations\`, each an add, a replace of the one fact \`old_text\` matches, or a remove of it, against target \`memory\` (the LivingMemory \`core\` ring of agent notes) or \`user\` (the \`user_core\` profile ring) (TARGETS, agents/core/memory_tool.py:61); a call with no operations reads both. The rings are reached only when cognition memory is on: the coordinator's \`_living_memory\` getter hands the tool the LivingMemory only when \`cog.sub_enabled("memory_enabled")\` holds (pinned by content at tests/test_h314_memory_tool.py:544-546), and a getter that yields nothing — memory off, safe mode, or a getter that fails (agents/core/memory_tool.py:429-441) — is refused \`memory_disabled\` (agents/core/memory_tool.py:469-471). Both rings come from one LivingMemory, so the enabled set is both or none: when memory is off the tool's offer says so through the H296 schema hook (OFF_DESCRIPTION, agents/core/memory_tool.py:459-460) and every call is refused \`memory_disabled\`, rather than the target enum being narrowed to an empty list. Every operation is checked on a working copy before anything is written (plan, agents/core/memory_tool.py:156): one line of at most 300 characters, the core block's own cut (MAX_FACT_CHARS, agents/core/memory_tool.py:63), with no control, format, private-use, surrogate or other invisible character (the quarantine.strip_format_chars set: variation selectors, Hangul fillers, U+034F, U+2800) (_clean_text, agents/core/memory_tool.py:112), scanned with the normalised injection scanner (_scan, agents/core/memory_tool.py:135), an old_text that matches exactly one fact, compared against the whitespace-normalised fact as the prompt shows it (_match, agents/core/memory_tool.py:144), no duplicate, and a full ring refusing an add instead of silently dropping its oldest fact; one refusal changes nothing. The rings are then written by a new compare-and-set (CoreMemory.compare_and_set, agents/core/cognition/memory.py:314) under the lock a forget clears them with, so a forget or another write that ran in between wins and nothing forgotten is written back; a second ring that fails puts the first back (_commit, agents/core/memory_tool.py:320). A compare-and-set that lost is refused \`memory_changed_meanwhile\`; a ring that cannot be saved is refused \`memory_write_failed\`. Only a clean owner turn at the operator surface writes: the resolver offers the tool to operator/owner alone, whatever llm.guest_tools says (OWNER_OPERATOR_TOOLS, agents/core/tool_profiles.py:102 and :243), the handler refuses any other posture (agents/core/memory_tool.py:449) and a turn whose origin is untrusted, an inbound message, web content or a flagged recall (agents/core/memory_tool.py:452), so an injected instruction cannot make itself permanent. Every write is committed and then recorded as an intent-log \`memory.write\` entry carrying the actor, the undo ref, the targets and per operation its target and action — never the text nor a hash of it, since an unsalted hash of a short fact is guessed back and the intent log survives a forget (agents/core/memory_tool.py:497). A record that cannot be made puts the rings back and records the put-back as \`memory.write_reverted\` (undo: \`memory.undo_reverted\`) with the same ref, naming exactly the rings it restored, because the intent log keeps a record whose save failed and writes it with its next one; a put-back that cannot be made (a ring moved again) is logged as an error and not recorded as one (_revert, agents/core/memory_tool.py:344; _record_put_back, agents/core/memory_tool.py:307). With no intent log nothing is written (_record, agents/core/memory_tool.py:299). The rings' previous contents are kept under the ref in a bounded undo store beside the rings (UndoStore, agents/core/memory_tool.py:228), which a forget deletes with them and which POST /api/admin/forget empties together with the live rings (clear_live_memory, agents/core/data_purge.py:429), so an undo during a forget cannot write the facts back. undo (agents/core/memory_tool.py:363) restores a write while the rings still hold what it wrote, by the same compare-and-set, recorded as \`memory.undo\`. The owner reads the rings and the writes undo would still restore — only those whose rings hold what they wrote (UndoStore.recent, agents/core/memory_tool.py:263) — at GET /api/memory/core (agents/core/routers/memory_kg.py:872) and undoes one at POST /api/memory/core/undo, admin-only (agents/core/routers/memory_kg.py:886). The Console's Long-Term Memory panel shows both rings and the recent writes with an undo each, and says when an undo is refused (LongTermMemoryPanel, frontend/src/panels/long-term-memory.tsx). A write that changes a ring leaves a \`memory_updated\` trail row with the changed targets and the actions, never text; a call that changes nothing leaves none (_record_event, agents/core/memory_tool.py:394).
