| <a id="h464"></a>H464 | Park a run on real async work instead of poking it | copy | Parțial | Reevaluat | Not reachable in production yet: - \*\*No process producer (owner decision 1; blocked on H302).\*\* Nothing in the hub starts run-owned background work and registers its pid: register_process has no caller outside tests. The best first producer is \`terminal_run\` with \`background: true\` on the local-host transport. It needs WorkRunLedger.run_for_task; a spawn with start_new_session, bounded log files and a held proc.wait() that records the exit code; a lifetime cap and killpg on cap, ESTOP or stop; a reaper for stopped runs; schema, approval-card and parity updates; and a KillMode in deploy/systemd/jarvis-hub.service (today a restart kills the child and the barrier clears as \`exited\`, indistinguishable from success). The owner must say whether the task/hook trigger is an accepted adaptation of Hermes's pid/session barrier, or whether a pid wait must be reachable for "equivalent". - \*\*Pid waits are unusable on macOS/BSD.\*\* There is no start token there, so every pid wait is refused \`pid_unprovable\`. The fix belongs in exec_cache.py (ctypes libproc proc_pidinfo(PROC_PIDTBSDINFO)) or in a producer-held Popen handle, and needs macOS hardware or a macOS CI runner to verify. - \*\*The judge's \`wait\` verdict and planner waits are not reachable in production (owner decision 2).\*\* WorkJudge.wait_probe needs a model rubric, and the shipped runtime passes no rubric, model planner or graders. Wiring one needs the owner's choice of local model and provider under H513 (auxiliary_request_scope, strict-local, security.data_training_ack) plus opt-in settings forced off in safe mode. Before any model planner, the rest of the intake arguments must be clamped: since H464c the task's kind is scope-checked as well as Action.kind, but the task's agent, title and payload still reach govern_enqueue unchanged. - \*\*No graders are wired in production.\*\* After the hub park clears, a run idles until its budget ends. Deterministic verifier and judge adapters belong to the company-mode grading work; they must reuse an existing verdict, because _grade has no try/except and a judge that raises after the verifier recorded leaves \`verdict_already_recorded\` / \`tick_failed\` on every later sweep. Deferred: - Wake-on-fire: a parked run resumes at the next scheduled sweep. - A \`job:\<id\>\` trigger. - A process output-pattern trigger (needs the process producer). - An owner-set wait like Hermes's \`/goal wait\` (owner decision 3): a clock or own-task wait only, never an owner-typed pid. - Waiting between checklist steps: the checklist still advances when a step's task is approved, not when it finishes. - A judge-sourced wait reserves no grading margin (only the hub's park does since H464c), so a judge wait that runs to the end of the budget still leaves the run ungraded. It is reachable only with a judge wait probe (owner decision 2). - The grading margin bounds one run's way back to a sweep, not a queue: with several runs due at once (max_concurrent 1), a parked run can lose the sweep's one slot after its cap. - A blocked run whose budget runs out is not settled (H464d settles only runs the sweep skips as budget_spent; a blocked one is skipped as blocked and its resume is refused once the owner answers), so it stays blocked on the record. - The HUD's live wait credit for an open ask runs to now; if the owner then edits the ask, the durable credit falls back to the last sweep that saw it open (at most one sweep's worth). - An owner stop of a working run is never closed out: request_stop moves it to \`stopping\` and settles only a second stop (agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:1436-1438), while ScheduleRuntime.due skips a \`stopping\` run (agents/core/autonomy/schedule_runtime.py:227-228), so the supervisor that would settle it is never ticked and the run reads \`stopping\` until the owner stops it again (reproduced on 03643762). Needs network: re-checking Hermes's goal-wait behaviour at the pinned commit 59b2aeef (hermes_cli/goals.py was not among the inspected upstream sources). Review residuals after round 3 (latent or bounded): a dropped grading sweep is not absorbed by the margin; a transient queue read during the per-sweep wait observation cuts approval-wait credit; a hold open when a run stops is never ended; an expired ask would be re-asked; the upgrade note's 're-approve' advice needs a new card; four test gaps (docs/handoff/2026-09-28-handover/h464-round3-brief.md). | <a id="h465"></a>H465 | Run the self-improvement review on demand | update | Echivalent | Reevaluat | Built in #1207 and fixed after six adversarial reviews: review-H465 (one major, seven minors, seven nits), review-H465b (three minors, six nits: a per-turn pass could still run beside /refine and borrow its label, a cut-off review read as nothing, and four mutants were unpinned) and review-H465c (three minors, six nits: a per-turn review cut off by the token cap was refunded, so a model that always truncates reviewed every turn; the settings the replies named could not be set; four survivors) and review-H465d (two minors, seven nits: a day of cut-offs made /refine name the wrong setting, seven real survivors, and a GA4 private key the CLI printed unmasked) and review-H465e (two minors, seven nits: the cut-off refusal on a day of mostly real reviews, nine real survivors, a budget read outside its bounds, a secret echoed by nerva config set, a pass in flight at midnight counted on the next day, a burst of turns past the cadence) and review-H465f (seven nits: a /refine refund keyed on the wrong day, a burst given too few passes, a later bracket closing an unclosed error, a fraction below one read as reviews off). All are fixed. Hermes' /refine \[focus\] forks the background memory and skill review against a snapshot of the conversation, so the live session is untouched. It refuses while a turn is in flight and reports the new or updated memories and skills back into the chat. Nerva's review engine is the per-turn BackgroundReviewer (strict-local, budgeted); it now also runs on demand. The command: - /refine \[focus\] is an owner command (agents/core/commands.py:377, registered at agents/core/commands.py:472). It answers from any channel's owner, and a guest is refused like any owner command. - The focus is one line of at most 200 characters. - It replies with what the review kept, one line per action (profile or core memory updated, corrections recorded, skill patch proposed, new skill quarantined, facts found but not kept because living memory is off). A skill change is said to wait in the Decision Inbox, and a new skill in the pending skills list. - Every non-run is named: a review already running, the daily budget spent, no local model answering (reviews never leave the machine), a model that spent its whole answer thinking (review_cut_off), a review cut off or malformed (review_unparsed, which names learning.review_max_tokens), reviews switched off (a daily budget of 0, reviews_off), the review outlasting its bound, nothing to review, no reviewer. One refusal added since this row's reviews has no wording of its own: a session whose history was imported from another assistant and is still tainted is refused foreign_history_not_promotable before the lease is looked at (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4021-4022), and the command answers it with the generic "The review did not run." line; the guard came with the owner-attested foreign-history resume (commit 8e1775bb), outside this row's claims and tests. An empty reply, a cut one, or a JSON object carrying none of the review's keys ({} or {"error": …}) is unparsed; only an object that says it found nothing reads as nothing worth keeping. A reply that parses as a review is the model's answer, whatever it opens with or mentions; only a reply that does not parse and is the local degraded message or opens with a bracketed \[… error …\] closed on its own line by its own bracket is a backend failure; an unclosed "\[Note: … error", or one a later \[1\] or link would close, is prose (review-H465e nit 7, review-H465f nit 3). - A local backend that is configured but down answers with a degraded string rather than raising. That is no review: it is reported as no local model and costs no budget (review-H465 M-1). A cut-off or malformed /refine costs none either; a per-turn pass cut off the same way does spend its unit, since the model ran to its cap, so the daily budget still bounds local GPU use when a model always truncates, and it is logged at INFO once a day, naming learning.review_max_tokens as the cause of a thinking cut-off and as a possible one of a malformed answer; a /refine cut-off does not use that line up. When such cut-offs are at least half of the day's spent units, /refine answers daily_budget_cut_off and says that, if they were cut off, the token cap is what to raise rather than the budget; one cut-off among real reviews is plain daily_budget (review-H465e m-1). A pass still waiting on the model at midnight refunds or counts against the day it spent its unit on, never the next (review-H465e nit 4), and GET /api/cognition/learning counts cut_offs_today. The unit is spent in run() after the budget is checked again there, so a burst of passes that all saw budget left in should_run cannot pass it; the cadence is checked there again too, so a burst of turns cannot pass it either (review-H465e nit 6), and a pass uses up only the turns that admitted it, so a burst gets the passes the same turns one at a time would (review-H465f nit 2) (_cut_off, agents/core/learning/background_review.py:513). - It runs whether or not the per-turn learning loop (cognition.review_enabled) is on: the owner asked, as Hermes' manual /refine does. Orchestrator.refine (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4001): - It reads a snapshot of the session's history and never writes to it. - The snapshot is conversation_snapshot (agents/core/learning/background_review.py:98): the newest turns whole and contiguous, each cut at 2,000 characters, up to 12,000 characters in all. Slash commands and the hub's replies to them are left out, so a chat of commands only has nothing to review. This replaces the per-turn review's last-6-turns, 300-character window for this path. - In flight, as it really behaves: every path that dispatches /refine holds the session's turn lease first. A /refine sent while another turn runs therefore waits for that turn (up to the lease's 180-second bound) and then reviews the conversation as it stands; it is not refused (review-H465 m-1 corrected the earlier claim). The review itself is bounded at 150 seconds (REFINE_TIMEOUT_S), below that wait, so the chat is busy for at most that long. - A direct caller holding no lease while another turn does is refused turn_in_flight: the lock is locked and the key is not among this context's held leases (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4026). No new in-flight set was added (critic note 1). - A review's result is the reviewer's last_result, which GET /api/cognition/learning shows (reviewer.status()); a refusal does not overwrite it. Each action is logged. The learning loop's knobs are declared settings (category learning, agents/core/settings_db.py:347): review_max_tokens (512, 1–32768), review_daily_budget (20, 0–1000), review_cadence (every_turn, every_n_turns, idle_gap), review_every_n (3), review_idle_gap_s (90) and review_max_facts (3), with the defaults the code already used, bounded in _LEARNING_INT_BOUNDS (agents/core/settings_db.py:949). The admin settings API, the HUD and nerva config set can change them; nerva config get shows a number named …max_tokens as the number it is, not masked as a credential, and masks every key the settings store encrypts (the GA4 service-account JSON among them), and nerva config set echoes such a value masked too (review-H465e nit 3). A model id is masked only under a hinted name: llm.default_model shows as typed. Every knob reads within its declared bounds whatever the stored row (a row from before the bounds, restored or hand-edited, reads as the default), the review's model call's token cap included (bounded_learning_int, agents/core/settings_db.py:964). A declared 0 for review_max_facts or review_idle_gap_s is honoured, not read as unset; corrections have a cap of their own (3), so a review_max_facts of 0 keeps no facts, still records corrections, and /refine says what it found but did not keep (_number, agents/core/learning/background_review.py:293). BackgroundReviewer.run_on_demand (agents/core/learning/background_review.py:335): - It skips the cadence gate but spends the daily budget, rolling over at midnight, and refunds it when no review was had (a model down, a cut-off answer, a timeout, a cancellation), on the day the pass spent it (review-H465f nit 1). A budget of 0 means no reviews and /refine says so (reviews_off); 2.5 reads as 2, and a value that is not a number or lies outside 0–1000 (text, infinity, a boolean, a hand-edited -3, a fraction below one) is logged once and 20 used (agents/core/learning/background_review.py:268). A per-turn pass that does not run leaves a DEBUG line naming why. It keeps the strict-local model, and is bounded at REFINE_TIMEOUT_S (150 s, below the lease's 180-second wait); no setting raises it. - It neither resets nor delays the per-turn cadence. It runs one at a time and never beside a per-turn review: a /refine while a per-turn pass runs is refused busy, and a per-turn pass that would start while /refine runs is skipped, not deferred. The exclusion is taken in run() itself (agents/core/learning/background_review.py:394), so a per-turn pass spawned before the /refine, still waiting on the memory lock, is refused on_demand when it enters. A cancelled review leaves no busy flag. - Its proposals, approval cards and new skills are labelled refine, not background_review; the label is passed down per pass, never kept on the instance. An injection-flagged correction is not recorded (on both paths). Facts found while living memory is off are counted after the injection scan, and said only to the owner who asked. - run gains a focus slot in REVIEW_PROMPT ("Focus for this review: …", absent when there is none, so the per-turn prompt is byte-identical) and a context bound, which this path sets to the snapshot's. Tests: tests/test_h465_refine.py (35 cases), tests/test_h465c_refine_review.py (9, the second review), tests/test_h465d_refine_review.py (31, the third review), tests/test_h465e_refine_review.py (37, the fourth review), tests/test_h465f_refine_review.py (34, the fifth review), tests/test_h465g_refine_review.py (18, the sixth review), tests/test_nerva_cli.py (a token budget shown unmasked), and tests/test_slash_commands.py pins the command in the owner's list. They cover: - the focus slot and its bound; - cadence skipped while the budget is spent, and the day's rollover; - one review at a time, and facts written; - the snapshot's bound, order, cutting and junk; - a whole snapshot reaching the prompt; - the reviewer receiving this session's snapshot while the session stays unchanged; - busy while another turn holds the lease, and not busy inside the command's own lease; - the empty and unavailable cases; - the owner-only command and its report, each named refusal, and /help; - the review's cases: a degraded reply is no review and costs no budget; the timeout; a cancelled review; mutual exclusion and the cadence kept; facts found with living memory off; an injected correction; the refine label; commands left out and contiguity; a chat of commands only; a refusal keeping the last result; the focus cut and where a new skill waits; a guest told /refine is the owner's. Mutation: 20 mutants; 18 were caught at once, and the other two after cases were added (the snapshot's bound reaching the prompt, the day rollover). The review's 28 mutants left four real survivors (a cancelled review's flag, the snapshot's contiguity, a refusal overwriting the last result, the focus cut); all are now caught. The first round's 19 mutants were all caught. The second review's 29 mutants left four real survivors (a new skill's label, a setting raising the bound, a garbage bound setting, a timeout's stored result): the bound setting is gone and the other two have cases. The third round's 14 mutants were all caught. The third review's 36 mutants (29 killed) left four real survivors (an empty reply, a reply cut after an inner }, a thinking cut-off's stored result, a cancelled /refine staying cancelled); all four have cases. That round's 22 mutants: 21 caught, one equivalent (an explicit unset check the except branch already covers, since removed). The fourth review's 40 mutants left seven real survivors (the documented values accepted, a search for an error anywhere, a /refine cut-off using up the day's line, a skip reason other than on_demand); each has a case, the day's line after a /refine only since the fifth round. That round's 19 mutants were all caught, two after their cases were added. The fifth review's 51 mutants left nine real survivors (the cut-off refusal's threshold, which pass logs the day's line, the orchestrator's bounded token cap, the rollover of cut_offs_today in both entry points, a /refine cut-off counted among them, the corrections cap, the found-not-kept count against injected and agent facts); each has a case. That round's 20 mutants were all caught. The sixth review's 40 mutants left two real survivors (a regex closed by a later bracket or line), each with a case now. This round's 6 mutants: four caught, two equivalent (the refund's day check and its reset, since nothing rolls the day while a /refine runs, and a /refine refunds at most once). Cerința structurală „fără gateway pornit” rămâne o divergență documentată: \`nerva send\` trece prin hub ca să existe IntentLog și rate-limit. Corpurile peste 4.000 de caractere sunt refuzate, nu fragmentate (Hermes fragmentează per platformă). Slack și Discord rămân reply-only (restul H018); email-ul e exclus deliberat. Nu există adresare \`platform:chat_id\[:thread\]\` / \`platform:#canal\` ca la Hermes: \`--channel telegram\` înseamnă întotdeauna chat-ul owner-ului. Precedența diverge deliberat: la Hermes argumentul câștigă în fața \`--file\`, aici ambele deodată e eroare de utilizare. Erorile nu au prefixul \`hermes send:\`. \`JobRunner._send\` își păstrează propria rezolvare a destinației (lot-ul jobs). Fără probă live pe un canal real din această sesiune: verificarea a fost prin hub fals și prin ChannelManager-ul real cu adaptoare false. | <a id="h481"></a>H481 | Refuse a catastrophic shell command no matter who approved it (hardline floor + risky-pattern tier + de-obfuscation) | update | Parțial | Reevaluat | \*\*The middle tier does not exist.\*\* The row asks for three stacked layers; this is the first, with its matching repaired (and repaired again in PR #1177). There is still no ~40-rule severity/reversibility-tagged risky-pattern catalogue feeding the approval card's description, so \`rm -rf ~/projects\` is neither hardline nor pattern-classified — re-checked 2026-09-19 on 494a13b2: \`hardline_match("rm -rf ~/projects")\` and \`hardline_match(\['rm','-rf','/home/x/projects'\])\` both return None, and the module carries no severity/reversibility/catalogue vocabulary at all — and the owner's card still says "run this argv" rather than "recursive delete", which the row's rationale names as the point. No user-editable \`approvals.deny\` fnmatch list at hardline level (no \`fnmatch\`/\`deny\` in the module). No parser limits that themselves hardline-block and save an oversized payload to a file for manual review (128k chars / 4096 separator-free / 25k segments); \`MAX_ARG_CHARS = 4000\` is argv validation, not a refusal. \*\*Variants Hermes produces and this still does not:\*\* NFKC normalisation, \`$HOME\`/\`$HERMES_HOME\` folding, grep-pattern span masking, and \`python -c\` / \`perl -e\` / \`node -e\` payload extraction — the last left alone on purpose, since \`jobs_scripts.snapshot_script\` legitimately builds \`\[sys.executable, '-I', '-c', source\]\`. \`$()\`/backtick substitution is now extracted in ONE place only: #1177's \`_substituted\` narrows a heredoc BODY line to its substitutions, so \`cat \<\<EOF\` / \`$(rm -rf /)\` / \`EOF\` refuses; an ordinary line is still not expanded, so \`echo $(rm -rf /)\` and a backtick \`rm -rf /\` inside an assignment return None (a \`$(mkfs.ext4 …)\` is caught only through \`_CMD\`'s \`(\` anchor). The row's own examples \`$(printf mkfs).ext4 /dev/sda\` and \`echo bWtmcw==\|base64 -d\|sh\` still return None. \*\*Gaps this module knows it still has, listed honestly rather than as a complete set:\*\* nesting deeper than \`_MAX_SHELL_DEPTH\` (depth-3 \`sh -c "sh -c 'sh -c …'"\` returns None, pinned by test); a quote at a word BOUNDARY (\`'mkfs.ext4' /dev/sda\`) rather than inside a word; \`powershell -EncodedCommand\` base64; a \`cmd /c\` payload split across several argv items; an obfuscated shell HEAD in argv form (\`\['s""h','-c',…\]\`), because the de-obfuscation pass runs after payload extraction and its output is not fed back through it; and, since #1177, two in the false-refusal direction — a \`case\` label with a leading \`(\` (\`(shutdown) echo bye ;;\`) is still read as a command, and a \`case\` nested inside another is not modelled: its inner first label IS stripped (\`case $1 in\\na) case $2 in\\nreboot) echo r ;;\\nesac ;;\\nesac\` went power_cycle→None), so the docstring's 'not handled' is about the region boundary, not a guaranteed refusal. \*\*Refusals #1177 cleared in the dangerous direction — closed by this slice (H481, 2026-09-22).\*\* The \`case\`-label strip fires only inside a real command-position \`case WORD in … esac\` region now, so \`(echo case in; reboot); echo esac\` and the \`$IFS\`-spliced \`(echo case in; mkfs.ext4$IFS/dev/sda); echo esac\` / \`wipefs$IFS-a$IFS/dev/sda\` refuse again; and \`_heredoc_feeds_a_shell\` now also sees a body a shell consumes AFTER the redirection through a pipe (\`cat \<\<EOF \| sh\`, \`cat \<\<EOF \| bash\`, \`cat \<\<EOF \| grep … \| sh\`) or via a file a shell later runs (\`cat \<\<'EOF' \>x.sh; sh x.sh\`), so those refuse — and, after the review round, so do \`(sh x.sh)\`, \`{ sh x.sh; }\`, \`if true; then sh x.sh; fi\`, \`cat x.sh \| sh\`, \`sh -c '. x.sh'\`, \`. x.sh\`, \`source x.sh\`, \`tee x.sh \<\<EOF; sh x.sh\`, a quoted \`\> "x.sh"\` target, \`sh /dev/stdin \<\<EOF\`, \`bash -c sh \<\<EOF\` and \`cat \<\<EOF \| eval "$(cat)"\`, each verified to run the body. Pinned in tests/test_local_transport.py, reproduced against /bin/sh, /bin/dash and /bin/bash first, and screened by a 671,995-case differential fuzz vs origin/main whose every difference is explained by the two changed mechanisms (numbers in the summary; the earlier \`refusals_cleared = 0\` claim is withdrawn). Still open in this direction, listed in \`_detection_variants\` and pinned as misses: a heredoc body written to a file run by a bare path (\`… \>x.sh; ./x.sh\`), by a variable-carried name (\`for f in x.sh; do sh $f; done\`) or by the environment (\`BASH_ENV=x.sh bash -c :\`); a heredoc opened inside a command substitution (\`eval "$(cat \<\<EOF …)"\`, read as quoted text); \`xargs -I{} sh -c '{}'\` (each line becomes the command line); and a \`;\` inside a \`( )\` group of a pipe stage (\`cat \<\<EOF \| (cd /tmp; sh)\`). \*\*Two pre-existing false positives are unchanged\*\* (\`git commit -m "fix;mkfs.ext4 handling"\` → mkfs; \`grep -r "(shutdown" docs/\` → power_cycle), and \`_PATH_PREFIX\` added a third class no approval can lift: a path to a script whose basename starts with a hardline name — \`./mkfs.sh\` (mkfs), \`./reboot.sh\`, \`./scripts/shutdown.sh --dry-run\`, \`/opt/app/bin/halt\` (power_cycle) — all None on 1c5054ea, all refused on 494a13b2 (bare \`reboot.sh\` already refused before; the prefix extends it to every path spelling). This slice left that (c) class unclosed on purpose: any name- or path-only rule that cleared \`./mkfs.sh\` or \`/opt/app/bin/halt\` would also clear a TRUE refusal — \`./mkfs.sh\` is structurally \`mkfs.\<suffix\>\` exactly like the real \`/sbin/mkfs.ext4\`, and \`/opt/app/bin/halt\` is \`\<path\>/\<hardline-name\>\` exactly like a copied \`/tmp/mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda\` — so it needs approval-context (is the target a workspace script or a real system binary) the pure static floor does not have. \*\*And a measured cost, re-measured after #1177 removed the breadth cap\*\* (\`_MAX_SHELL_EXPANSIONS\` and the \`MAX_ARG_CHARS\` re-expansion guard are gone; every level-1 payload is unwrapped again): on a maximal 64x4000-character argv the pass is roughly unchanged (79.6 ms on the pre-#1177 module vs 82.3 ms after, same machine, best of 5), but a command made of 2,000 nested \`sh -c "sh -c 'echo ok'"\` segments (57k chars) goes from 196 ms to 380 ms — synchronous, on the event loop, before every exec. The docstring's linear-in-input argument holds (each level's payloads are disjoint substrings); an independent re-run on another machine saw 79.0→80.6 ms and 125→151 ms, so the constant grows for nested input but the factor is machine-dependent and no test pins either number. This slice's first pass claimed no measurable cost on that maximal 64x4000-character argv (78.7 → 78.4 ms); the review showed the claim held only for input with no \`case\` word and never exercised the redirect-target branch, which was quadratic. Re-measured after the review round (best of 3, same machine, origin/main → this branch): the maximal 64x4000 argv 62.0 → 58.6 ms; the same argv filled with case/in prose 18,207 → 105 ms (main's own \`\\bcase\\b.\*?\\besac\\b\` was super-linear there too); 4000 chars of \`case x in\` 21.6 → 6.5 ms; eight 4000-char argv items of prose 316 → 14 ms; 400 \`cat \<\<EOF \| sh\` blocks (12 KB) 39.8 → 64.9 ms; 400 \`cat \<\<E \>x\` blocks in 4000 chars 25 → 39 ms (2,471 ms on the first pass); 1,600 such blocks (33.6 KB) 132 → 201 ms (97.5 s on the first pass); 2,000 nested \`sh -c\` segments 146 → 148 ms; 300 real \`case\` statements 57 → 60 ms. The heredoc-with-target shapes cost about 1.5x main, linear, because the statement lines after a heredoc are tokenised once and shared; nothing else pays. Six test items pin wall-clock bounds (0.25–2 s) two orders of magnitude above these; no test pins a ratio. \*\*Adversarial review of the original slice found four more defects, all fixed and each reproduced first\*\* against real /bin/sh, /bin/dash and /bin/bash: (1) \`_shell_c_payloads\` demanded the word after the wrappers BE the shell, so \`env FOO=1 sh -c 'mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda'\` — and \`sudo -u root sh -c …\`, \`nice -n 10 sh -c …\` — skipped the whole \`sh -c\` screening while deleting \`FOO=1 \` made the same string \`hardline_denied:mkfs\`; \`_CMD\` had been widened for that assignment prefix and the unwrapper had not. (2) \`_unquoted_lines\` read a backslash-newline as a statement separator when it is a line CONTINUATION, so \`mk\\\` + newline + \`fs.ext4 /dev/sda\`, which all three shells splice into \`mkfs.ext4\`, was seen as two harmless fragments. (3) every heredoc body line became a command position, so \`cat \> x.yaml \<\<'EOF'\` / \`shutdown: graceful\` / \`EOF\` was refused as \`power_cycle\`; body lines were joined as data in the flat text. \*\*#1177's second review showed that fix was incomplete in three ways, all closed there:\*\* \`segments\` still tokenised every body line, so \`cat \> README.md \<\<'EOF'\` / \`rm -rf / will destroy the box\` / \`EOF\` stayed a \`recursive_root_removal\` refusal; the rule had no exception for a heredoc a SHELL consumes, so \`bash \<\<EOF\` / \`mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda\` / \`EOF\` returned None (a bypass the heredoc work itself opened); and any \`\<\<\` — inside quotes, inside \`$(( ))\`, a \`\<\<\<\` here-string, or with a delimiter that never returns — opened a heredoc and switched the newline screening off for every following line. (4) \`{\` anchored bare, so \`jq '{reboot: .needs_reboot}'\` was a \`power_cycle\` refusal; POSIX requires whitespace after \`{\` for a brace group, and \`{ mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda; }\` is still refused. Each fix is red-proofed on its own. [d1](../agents/core/environments/terminal_contract.py) [d2](../tests/test_local_transport.py) |

| <a id="h495"></a>H495 | Never let a credential reach a log, a transcript, an approval card or an export | update | Parțial | Reevaluat | This is one of the row's seven paths. Hermes applies \`redact.py\` to logs, verbose output, tool output, approval prompts, gateway messages, transcripts and memory; this slice covers LOGS. Still owed, and the rationale calls them the part that matters most: the hash-chained audit DB (a \`cat .env\` from \`terminal_run\` still writes a live credential into an append-only log that by design cannot be edited), the decision-inbox approval card the owner reads on a phone, task payloads, terminal output, and the observability exports — which Hermes scrubs unconditionally with no knob, returning \`\[redaction-unavailable\]\` rather than raw text. Also absent: the second mask mode (a syntactically INVALID \`«redacted:ghp_…»\` sentinel for file reads, so an agent cannot write a masked-but-plausible key back and silently kill the credential), \`code_file=True\` sparing source constants, \`_mask_control_split_tokens()\` for tokens smuggled across ANSI/zero-width characters, and the shared \`.env\` basename list. The two silent-degradation paths named at review are now CLOSED, after the SAST gate forced the question: a handler whose \`addFilter\` fails is counted and published through \`uncovered_handler_count()\` and a warning naming how many handlers are writing unredacted, and a \`loggerDict\` walk that raises warns that coverage fell back to root-only. The one silent swallow left is the filter's own last-ditch blank (\`# nosec B110\`), where a \`logging.Filter\` that raises would take down the caller's log call and the scanner has already failed. \`install_log_redaction()\` remains exported although the \`everywhere\` variant is what production uses. \*\*A later slice's full-suite run surfaced one more thing about this control, recorded here rather than fixed:\*\* the scanner's \`high_entropy_secret\` pattern matches an ordinary filesystem path. Under \`-n auto --dist loadfile\` a warning naming a pytest tmp file arrived as \`truncated: \[REDACTED:high_entropy_secret\].md\`, which is what a real operator would see when a log line names a file with a long random-looking segment — a debuggability cost the module docstring already warns about in general terms, now with a concrete case. Separately, \`setup_logging()\` installs the filter on every handler of every logger and nothing took it back off, so every later test on the same xdist worker ran under a live redactor. The installer is PRODUCTION code, not the tests: \`agents/run.py\` calls \`setup_logging()\` at module level, so importing it installs the filter during pytest COLLECTION — before any fixture runs — and eight test files import it; \`agents/web.py\` calls it from the FastAPI lifespan, so any test that drives the app installs it again; five test files call it directly on top of that. There is no list of leaking files to fix. The cleanup therefore lives in \`tests/conftest.py\` as an autouse fixture that strips unconditionally BEFORE each test as well as after — a snapshot-and-restore fixture, which is what the two neighbouring isolation fixtures do and what this was first written as, treats a collection-time install as pre-existing and preserves it for the life of the worker. That version went green locally and RED in CI on exactly the test it was meant to fix. The first attempt at it matched by \`isinstance\` and silently did nothing: \`agents/\` is on \`sys.path\`, so \`core.security.log_redaction\` and \`agents.core.security.log_redaction\` are two module objects over this one file with two distinct \`SecretRedactionFilter\` classes, and the root handler was carrying the other one. The match is by class name now, and four paired tests pin both halves — including the alternate import path, which is the case the first attempt missed. Slack and Discord have no deeplink path and gate through the same gateway instance. Still outstanding, from the row itself: (b) \*no lockout after N failed attempts\* — the row wants a 1 h lockout after 5 failed approvals, checked BEFORE the pending lookup so a code already in flight cannot be brute-forced past it; there is still only a rate limit and an in-memory guess budget, both of which reset on restart. (d) is half closed: the chat command registry does split owner and user tiers on channels — \`_channel_principal\` makes only a configured owner sender an admin principal and every ADMIN-tier command refuses anyone else with "owner command" (agents/core/commands.py:159-165) — so a paired stranger gets only the user-tier commands; still missing is the always-allowed floor's \`whoami\` (no such command exists), so the row's \`{help, whoami}\` floor is not met. \*\*Unaddressed from the Hermes column:\*\* pairing-code GENERATION (8 characters from a 32-char unambiguous alphabet via \`secrets.choice\`) and the code's 1 h TTL — the code here never expires; "max 3 pending per platform" (the store bounds 200 globally); "1 request per user per 10 min" (it is 5); \`unauthorized_dm_behavior\` treating inbox-shaped platforms differently from chat-shaped ones; and the ordered authorization union (allow-all flag → pairing approvals → per-platform allowlist → global allowlist → global allow-all → default DENY), which is still an ad-hoc sequence in \`is_allowed\`/\`gate_inbound\`. \*\*Two honest limits of the second slice.\*\* The store itself still has no defence against a second instance — the guarantee is one instance per process by construction, and the premise test says so in words. And an install that had relocated its data root (\`JARVIS_HOME\`) and paired senders through the HUD kept them in \`\<cwd\>/memory_logs/sender_pairing.json\`; the store now opens under the data root, so those senders are held once more until re-approved (the owner's allowlisted ids never lived in that file and are unaffected). \*\*And the limit carried from the first slice.\*\* Stretching is a work factor, not a wall: a four-digit code goes from milliseconds to minutes, an eight-character mixed-alphabet code becomes infeasible, and \*\*nothing enforces a floor on what the owner types\*\* — \`PairingCodeBody\` caps the length at 128 and sets no minimum — while generating the code for them, the row's own prescription, is not implemented. | <a id="h501"></a>H501 | Warn about a dangerous deployment posture before it becomes an incident | update | Echivalent | Reevaluat | Nerva now warns about a dangerous host posture, as Hermes does, on top of a network half that was already stronger. assert_safe_bind (agents/core/boot_guards.py) still refuses an unauthenticated non-loopback bind and prints the exact env vars that fix it, and GET /api/security/posture still reports the secrets backend, skill signing, sandbox isolation and guardrails honestly. agents/core/host_posture.py adds the host half: three read-only checks that never block and never change anything, each answering ok, warn or unknown (it could not tell, never a false green), with a reason, what it saw and the fix. check_root (agents/core/host_posture.py:71) warns when the process runs as root (euid 0) on any host, headless included, or elevated on Windows (IsUserAnAdmin). check_sshd (agents/core/host_posture.py:168) reads /etc/ssh/sshd_config the way sshd does (_SshdScan, agents/core/host_posture.py:120): Include files are read in place, relative paths from /etc/ssh, each pattern's hits in lexical order, at most 16 deep; Keyword value, Keyword=value and trailing comments are accepted and keywords and values are case-insensitive; the first PasswordAuthentication outside a Match block wins, so a drop-in Included at the top overrides the main file; a Match block (to the end of its file, an Include inside it conditional) never sets the global value but a Match block that turns passwords on warns too; an absent directive is the sshd default yes and warns; no sshd_config is ok; an unreadable file is unknown unless the answer was read elsewhere; an unrecognised value is unknown. check_container_storage (agents/core/host_posture.py:241) detects a container (/.dockerenv, /run/.containerenv, or a docker, kubepods, containerd, libpod or lxc cgroup of PID 1, in_container) and then finds the mount the data root (resolved through symlinks) lives on in /proc/self/mountinfo (parse_mountinfo with its octal escapes, mount_of taking the longest containing mount point and the later of two stacked mounts): the container's own root filesystem or a tmpfs warns, a volume or bind mount is ok, no mountinfo or no mount is unknown. run_checks and report (agents/core/host_posture.py:273, :287) run the three independently, a failing check becoming an unknown row. The hub logs each warning once per process at start, after logging is set up, off the event loop (log_startup, agents/web.py lifespan). GET /api/security/posture (admin) gains host: the three findings and a warnings count (agents/core/routers/security.py). python scripts/doctor.py and nerva doctor show them as the advisory rows host_not_root, sshd_no_passwords and container_storage at the end of the report: a warning is warn with the fix and never fails the verdict, a check that could not tell or could not run is skip, never ok (check_host_posture, scripts/doctor.py:247). The module is stdlib only so the doctor can use it on a broken install. The shipped Dockerfile has no USER, so a stock container now shows the root warning; running the image as a non-root user is left to the deploy. Tests: tests/test_h501_host_posture.py (42), with real sshd_config trees in a temporary directory (drop-ins read first and last, lexical order, absolute and quoted Includes, Match blocks in the main and in an included file, a trailing comment naming a file, an Include loop) and real mountinfo text. 55 mutants: 53 killed after five cases were added; the other two were dead code, removed. Re-read 2026-10-10 after two pinned files drifted. The mechanism files (agents/core/host_posture.py, agents/core/boot_guards.py, scripts/doctor.py, tests/test_h501_host_posture.py) hold their pins and every citation above resolves unchanged. agents/core/routers/security.py changed by one hunk that widens DataHandlingAck.target with the video roles; the posture route still returns the host findings (agents/core/routers/security.py:396). agents/web.py changed by auth-event auditing, channel pending handlers and ntfy opt-in hunks, none of which mention the posture checks; the startup warning is still logged off the event loop (agents/web.py:497). tests/test_h501_host_posture.py passes (42) and the full backend suite is green on this head. Verdict unchanged. [d1](../agents/core/host_posture.py) [d2](../agents/core/boot_guards.py) [d3](../agents/core/routers/security.py) |
| <a id="h502"></a>H502 | Refuse an MCP server entry that is a backdoor wearing an MCP costume, and never hand one the owner's keys | copy | Parțial | Reevaluat | \*\*The documented per-server \`env\` migration path does not exist as a reachable surface.\*\* \`MCPServerConfig\` has no \`env\` field (\`routers/mcp.py:145-157\`, no \`model_config\`), \`POST /api/admin/mcp\` drops the key (pydantic's default \`extra="ignore"\`), and neither \`to_config\` (\`client.py:798-812\`) nor \`load_from_config\` (\`:814-849\`) writes or reads one — the module docstring says as much at \`client.py:41-45\`. The only remedy an owner can actually reach is the \*\*host-wide\*\* \`JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ALLOWED_ENV\` (\`:92-98\`, "Host-wide, not per-server"), which is a strictly weaker grant than the per-server one the docs describe: an owner whose forge server needs \`GITHUB_TOKEN\` must allow it for every stdio server on the host. Whether to ship on that or build the per-server surface first is a product decision, written up as \`docs/OWNER_TASKS.md\` §P28.3 with both options. \*\*Related and also owner-level:\*\* \`XAUTHORITY\` and \`DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS\` are both on \`STDIO_ENV_ALLOWLIST\` (\`client.py:169\`), and today one is listed-but-silently-dropped (\`_SECRET_LIKE\` at \`:174-176\` matches the \`AUTH\` in \`XAUTHORITY\`) while the other is listed-and-handed-over — they should be consistent in one direction or the other. \*\*And the honest ceiling, stated wherever the guarantee is:\*\* this is \*\*defence in depth, not a security boundary\*\*, and since #1179 the module states that ceiling by TWO routes rather than one (\`client.py:17-36\`). The child is same-UID with no namespace, so a server that can run a subprocess reads the withheld variables straight out of \`/proc/\<ppid\>/environ\`; and the baseline narrows the \*\*filesystem\*\* not at all — \`cwd\` defaults to the hub's own working directory, so \`open(".env")\` hands back exactly the keys that were withheld, which \`cwd_secret_files()\` now says out loud at connect (WARNING, filenames only, \`client.py:565-571\`) rather than leaving the owner to infer a protection from the withheld count alone. What the baseline buys is that a \*careless\* or \*curious\* server does not get them by accident, and that an owner's \`JARVIS_\*\` settings are not ambient in a third party's process. It does not stop an adversary, and the row says so rather than implying otherwise; closing the filesystem route as well as the \`/proc\` one needs real process isolation (separate UID, namespace or container — \`client.py:33-36\`), which is not shipped. \*\*Unaddressed from the row:\*\* there is no refusal of an MCP entry that is a backdoor wearing an MCP costume — no command allow-listing, no signature or provenance check on the spawned binary (the docstring itself calls the screener "still-unshipped", \`client.py:34\`), and \`POST /api/admin/mcp\` still stores \`req.command\` verbatim after checking only transport, trust tier, tool-filter shape and bounds, and duplicate name (\`routers/mcp.py:188-241\`, \`:184\`); the only shape check is \`_command_argv()\`'s shell-metacharacter/NUL refusal at connect (\`client.py:519-529\`), which is not a screener. #1179 changed none of this — it explicitly chose disclosure over refusal. This slice hardens what the child \*receives\*; the row also asks who the child is allowed to \*be\*. | <a id="h503"></a>H503 | Unpack an archive from another machine without letting it write outside the destination | update | Echivalent | Reevaluat | archive_safe is the only module in Nerva that reads an archive. Backup verify and restore unpack through extract_tar_path (agents/core/archive_safe.py:573; agents/core/backup.py:598, agents/core/backup.py:667). Marketplace install_from_zip unpacks through extract_zip_bytes (agents/core/archive_safe.py:637; agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:816). The old backup._safe_extract and the marketplace _safe_targets+extractall pass are gone. An AST scan (tests/test_archive_safe.py:702, with probes at tests/test_archive_safe.py:688) fails when any other product module imports tarfile or zipfile outside a write-only allowlist, opens an archive for reading or calls an extract-family method. normalize_member (agents/core/archive_safe.py:122) folds backslash to '/' first. It then refuses empty, NUL, POSIX-absolute, Windows-absolute, UNC and drive-lettered names, and any '..' or empty part. Only regular files and directories are written. Symlink, hardlink, device, fifo and sparse tar members raise (agents/core/archive_safe.py:504), and so do symlink, device, fifo, socket and encrypted zip entries (agents/core/archive_safe.py:596). _Planner (agents/core/archive_safe.py:182) validates every member before the first write: name, type, in-archive conflicts and duplicates, member count and declared bytes (agents/core/archive_safe.py:257). It also checks the destination's existing content (agents/core/archive_safe.py:286): a link on the way to a member is refused, and so is a directory where a file goes (tests/test_archive_safe.py:365, tests/test_backup.py:471). The pre-scan reads the stream to its end (agents/core/archive_safe.py:522), so a bad gzip CRC, trailing data or a corrupt header part-way through is a refusal, not a shortened tree (tests/test_archive_safe.py:482, tests/test_archive_safe.py:517). Bytes are counted again while streaming (agents/core/archive_safe.py:389). The byte budget is clamped to free space plus the blocks of the single-link files the archive replaces (agents/core/archive_safe.py:314), so an in-place --force restore fits (tests/test_backup.py:443). PAX and GNU long-name header payloads are capped before tarfile reads them, 1 MiB each and 256 MiB in total (agents/core/archive_safe.py:461, agents/core/archive_safe.py:483; tests/test_backup.py:515). A link or hardlinked name at a member's path is unlinked and the file is created O_EXCL\|O_NOFOLLOW, never written through (agents/core/archive_safe.py:373; tests/test_archive_safe.py:323, tests/test_archive_safe.py:349). Backups take their caps from JARVIS_BACKUP_MAX_MEMBERS and JARVIS_BACKUP_MAX_BYTES (agents/core/backup.py:86); skill packages use SKILL_PACKAGE_LIMITS (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:42). On the producing side, create_backup writes both the encrypted and the plaintext branch through atomic_write, a sibling temp file that is fsynced and then os.replace'd (agents/core/archive_safe.py:654; agents/core/backup.py:415, agents/core/backup.py:420). Archives are GNU-format tar (agents/core/backup.py:474). The export walk skips symlinks (agents/core/archive_safe.py:715; agents/core/backup.py:401). publish_skill uses it on the staged copy it signs (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:392); the copy itself is built from the bytes of one source snapshot, which refuses a linked folder, a link or non-regular member and a file that changed while read (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:375), which has its own test (tests/test_marketplace_governance_hf12_12.py:219). Every other name, hardlinked ones included, is archived as its own regular member (agents/core/backup.py:434, agents/core/backup.py:458; tests/test_backup.py:388). verify and restore compare the manifest's file_count with what the archive held (agents/core/backup.py:625; tests/test_backup.py:430). install_from_zip stages inside skills_dir, runs the signature gate there, and only then renames the tree into place (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:854, agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:885). A non-zip upload is a 400 refusal (tests/test_marketplace_governance_hf12_12.py:194). Staging left by a killed install is swept once it is an hour old (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:773; tests/test_marketplace_governance_hf12_12.py:203). Restore stays an operator CLI action. It prints 'partial restore' when a failure came after the first write (agents/core/backup.py:716) and 'nothing restored' only for a pre-scan refusal (agents/core/backup.py:722). tests/test_backup.py:606 pins that no product module, script or subprocess caller reaches it. The pre-scan also refuses a component longer than the destination's NAME_MAX or a path past PATH_MAX, which the existing-path walk cannot see under a new directory (agents/core/archive_safe.py:251; tests/test_archive_safe.py:726), and a write the destination refuses mid-restore (permissions, a full disk) is a named ArchiveRejected marked partial, never a traceback (agents/core/archive_safe.py:445; tests/test_archive_safe.py:738). A restore leaves the archive's manifest in the target; create_backup never archives a top-level backup_manifest.json from the data root (agents/core/backup.py:482), so a backup of a restored root carries one manifest and verifies, restores and serves the forget purge's verified pre-snapshot (tests/test_backup.py:636, tests/test_backup.py:675). A backup of a restored root made before this change carries that name twice; verify and restore accept exactly that one repeat, last wins as tarfile resolved it, and count the dropped copy against the manifest's file_count (agents/core/backup.py:599, agents/core/backup.py:642; tests/test_backup.py:651). The repeat is bounded: the dropped copy still counts against the member and byte caps, and a third copy or any other duplicate is refused (agents/core/archive_safe.py:220, agents/core/archive_safe.py:223; tests/test_archive_safe.py:768, tests/test_archive_safe.py:775, tests/test_archive_safe.py:790). Known limit: backups made on main from a data root holding a symlink or hardlink fail verify and restore by design. [d1](../agents/core/archive_safe.py) [d2](../agents/core/backup.py) [d3](../agents/core/skills/marketplace.py) |
| <a id="h504"></a>H504 | Fail loudly when TLS trust is misconfigured instead of silently not verifying | update | Echivalent | Reevaluat | Startup validates all configured CA bundle paths and certifi, loads them through SSLContext, requires actual certificates, and supplies named repair instructions. Model egress uses an explicit trust context; invalid CA paths never imply verify=False. Per-target insecure overrides are explicit, loudly logged and ignored in hardened mode. Functional adaptation retained from the existing implementation: custom bundles may contain a valid short EC or pinned self-signed certificate; the 1024-byte minimum is reserved for the multi-root certifi bundle. Actual SSL parsing and certificate presence validate custom trust material instead of rejecting a valid anchor by byte length. All 45 TLS tests plus 22 plugin-egress tests pass, including real generated certificates and a loopback HTTPS server that fails without and succeeds with the owner CA. No external-provider connection or host trust-store change was performed. Batch-03 collateral review (2026-10-10): the changed evidence paths were compared with their previously current preimages. H329 adds strict global/channel owner switches and exact human-approved re-enable; H299/H397 add result-aware default-advisory stalls. This review preserves the existing contract verdict and remaining limits; unrelated stale pins remain unchanged. Current verification and limits are recorded in docs/plans/2026-10-10-hermes-closure-03.md. Batch-04 bounded collateral review (2026-10-10): changed evidence was checked against its previously current preimage; the existing verdict and remaining limits remain valid. Details are in the batch-04 runtime, surface and history collateral reviews. Batch-05 bounded collateral review (2026-10-10): the H002 usage/terminal-stop changes and additive response fixtures were checked against previously current evidence. Existing verdicts and remaining limits are preserved; already-stale pins remain untouched. See the batch-05 integration and root collateral reports. | <a id="h506"></a>H506 | Treat files that steer future runs as a distinct always-ask class, on the way in and on the way out | copy | Parțial | Reevaluat | \*\*The read half now covers two of the three Nerva loaders and none of the external ones — the row stays partial.\*\* H506 requires the same file class to be scanned at context-load time with a positive match replaced by \`\[BLOCKED: … Content not loaded.\]\`. What holds: SOUL.md / SOUL.local.md through \`Agent._scan_soul_body\` (H387's evidence, not this row's — per-line quarantine over the union of raw and normalised copies, cross-line wraps, whole-body drop above the ratio; the U+200B and U+0007 spellings after 'now' are pinned in this row's own test file), and HEARTBEAT.md / HEARTBEAT.local.md through \`scan_heartbeat_config\`, entry refused rather than line-stubbed. \*\*Precisely what is not covered, stated rather than smoothed over:\*\* the Markdown body after the front-matter is discarded by \`_parse_heartbeat\` and reaches no model, log or scheduler, so it is not scanned — \`test_the_prose_body_is_not_loaded_and_therefore_not_scanned\` is the tripwire a loader that starts reading it must flip; no heartbeat text is model input today — the checklist strings are keyword-routed to skills with constant arguments and echoed into a logged run summary — so the scan guards the mapping the loader hands to the agent, not a live prompt path; the keyword scanner is literal after normalisation, so a Cyrillic homoglyph ('Іgnore'), a combining overlay, markdown emphasis inside a phrase ('Ignore _all_ previous') and a phrase split across two checklist items still scan clean — a confusables fold is a separate \`quarantine.py\` slice, and the homoglyph is pinned as a tripwire in this row's test file; and the SOUL cross-line path (\`_wrapped_injection_hits\`) builds its own normalised copy inside \`agent.py\`, so a blank-instead-of-space spelling that ALSO wraps across lines is not covered there (agent.py is untouched here; it is H387's evidence, being re-evaluated by a sibling stream). \*\*Adjacent, pre-existing, NOT fixed:\*\* the orchestrator's \`load_from_config\` overwrites every shipped HEARTBEAT.md cron+checklist with the agents.yaml interval (all twelve shipped agents carry one), so at runtime \`Agent.run_heartbeat\` finds no checklist and returns None for the shipped roster — the loader semantics this row describes are what the code does, not what the shipped agents experience (recorded as a separate task); \`load_all\` keys the config by the front-matter's own \`agent\` field, so a clean \`HEARTBEAT.local.md\` in one agent's directory that says \`agent: jarvis\` replaces Jarvis's schedule (a refused file cannot — the verdict is keyed by directory); and \`enabled: false\` is parsed and never honoured. Still open on the read side: AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / GEMINI.md / \`.cursorrules\` / \`\*.mdc\` are read by the external harnesses rather than by Nerva, so 'the same file class on the way in' is not met for them. The write-side deviations stand as before: the row's \*"fails closed on a config read error"\* clause has no analogue because the roster is a hard-coded frozenset; \`allow_session=False\` holds only incidentally through the gated toolrpc \`autonomy_level="ask"\` intake, with nothing pinning it; and the class covers \`file_write\`/\`file_delete\` only — the terminal contract, the skill importer and the desktop operator are outside it. Unverified, stated as such: whether the Telegram decision card and the HUD decision inbox render the write-side notice verbatim, and whether any HUD renders the \`blocked\` list (the API carries it; \`frontend/src/gap.tsx\` and \`agents/web/static/systems.js\` read \`heartbeats\` only). \`_mutate\`'s floor remains lifted by a caller-supplied \`approved=True\` by design. | <a id="h507"></a>H507 | Warn the model when the code it just wrote contains a known-dangerous pattern | copy | Echivalent | Reevaluat | Code the agent writes is checked against a table of known-dangerous patterns, and the findings go back to the model and the owner. Nothing is ever refused. agents/core/code_guidance.py holds 26 rules (RULES, agents/core/code_guidance.py:89), each scoped to the file types it applies to. They cover unsafe deserialization (pickle/dill/joblib/marshal loads; yaml.load without SafeLoader, and yaml.unsafe_load; torch.load without weights_only=True); command and code injection (os.system/popen, shell=True, Python eval/exec, JS eval and new Function, child_process.exec and execSync, require('child_process').exec, a bare exec( in a file that imports child_process, a Go exec.Command of a shell); SQL built from an f-string or \`%\`; tempfile.mktemp; XSS sinks (innerHTML/outerHTML assignment, document.write, dangerouslySetInnerHTML); and crypto and TLS footguns (ECB mode, createCipher without an IV on any receiver, verify=False, unverified SSL contexts, CERT_NONE, rejectUnauthorized: false, NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0, InsecureSkipVerify: true, md5/sha1 over a password). They also cover XXE parser flags and a remote \`\<script\>\` without integrity=. A separate check (_workflow_findings, agents/core/code_guidance.py:189) flags \`${{ github.event.\* }}\` inside a GitHub Actions \`run:\` step, on the run line or in its \`\|\`/\`\>\` block, whose column is the run key's own, so a \`- run: \|\` step's env:, with: and if: keys end it and are never flagged. The guards keep the usual false positives quiet: \`model.eval()\` and \`obj.eval()\`, \`def eval(\`, \`yaml.load(..., Loader=SafeLoader)\`, \`torch.load(..., weights_only=True)\`, \`regex.exec()\`, an \`===\` comparison with innerHTML, \`hashlib.md5(data)\`, a script with integrity=, whole-line comments and non-code files. Every rule is linear: a guard reads the call's balanced arguments across lines, at most MAX_CALL_CHARS (400) of them and at most MAX_CALLS_PER_LINE (8) calls a line (_call_args, agents/core/code_guidance.py:211; _guarded, agents/core/code_guidance.py:226), or the tag it matched. scan (agents/core/code_guidance.py:265) returns \`{rule, line, message}\`, at most 20 findings over the first 1 MB, with lines split at \`\\n\` only (CRLF and CR normalised), and stops after SCAN_SECONDS (0.5 s; agents/core/code_guidance.py:50); a scan cut by size or time ends with a \`scan-incomplete\` finding at the first line it did not finish, so a cut scan never reads as clean. \`.env\`, \`.env.\*\` and the shell dotfiles are scanned as shell. The findings go to five places. On the file_write approval card, FileTools.classify_mutation (agents/core/file_tools.py:1277) adds \`code_warnings\` (rule@line, at most 200 characters), \`code_warning_count\` and a title notice (\`code not fully scanned\` when a limit cut it), scanning the name as spelled and the file the write lands on (a symlink, a \`./\` or \`//\` spelling; labels, agents/core/code_guidance.py:296, names each finding once and in line order); it never sets a class, so H506's approval binding is untouched, and an instruction-file notice and the warning share the title. The gated call's \`approval_required\` answer carries \`code_warnings\`/\`code_warning_count\` (_ANSWER_LABEL_KEYS, agents/core/tool_rpc.py:200), and the tool loop's pause reply names them as warnings, not refusals (_approval_reply, agents/core/agent_runtime.py:1758): the loop ends the turn there, so the model reads them on its next turn and the owner at once. On an ungated write's result (FileTools.write_file, agents/core/file_tools.py:1024), the model reads \`code_warnings\` with a \`code_guidance\` note that they are warnings; an approved write's result lands on the approved task's record, which no model turn reads. A refused write carries none, and a failing scan never fails a write. For a marketplace install (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:858; install and install-zip answer \`code_warnings\` when there are any, agents/core/routers/skills.py:490) and a generated skill (agents/core/skills/loader.py:1211), scan_tree (agents/core/code_guidance.py:340) walks the folder, skipping symlinks; only code files count toward its 200-file bound, a file past 1 MB is read as cut, the whole walk stops after TREE_SECONDS (2 s), and the file a bound stops at gets a \`scan-incomplete\` finding. skill_propose answers the generated skill's \`code_warnings\` (agents/core/skills/tools.py:493), and generate_skill resets them first (agents/core/skills/loader.py:1051), so a skipped generation never keeps another's; the background-review and \[learn:\] generation paths only log them (their main.py is a fixed template). The owner's switch is \`security.code_guidance\` (read by enabled, agents/core/code_guidance.py:161: on by default, only an explicit off turns it off and an unreadable store keeps it on; the settings row is seeded on in settings_db DEFAULTS, and safe mode forces it back on: safe_mode.FORCED_SETTINGS, agents/core/safe_mode.py:110). An aliased child_process module (\`cp.exec\`) is not flagged. tests/test_h507_code_guidance.py (136 cases) covers every rule firing, the guard cases, the cross-language scoping, the finding shape, the table size, the workflow rule with a blank line in a block and every non-run key, the bounds, the labels, the switch, the real ToolRPC card and approved execution, a clean and a non-code write, the shared instruction notice, a failing scan, a refused write, scan_tree (symlink, bounds, switch), generation, install with the route, and the setting row. The review round added crafted megabytes (one per quadratic rule) scanned in under a second and a card labelled promptly through the ToolRPC intake, the time and size cuts, the pause reply driven through the agent loop, skill_propose's warnings and the reset, the symlink and path spellings, a package padded with assets, the \`- run: \|\` block, the wrapped and nested calls, the child_process and createCipher spellings, CR/form-feed/U+2028 lines, the dotfiles and the safe-mode switch. The review round's 44 mutants were all killed, ten after seven cases were added. Independent #1233 review (historical scope): Code the agent writes is checked against a table of known-dangerous patterns, and the findings go back to the model and the owner. Nothing is ever refused. agents/core/code_guidance.py holds 26 rules (RULES, agents/core/code_guidance.py:89), each scoped to the file types it applies to. They cover unsafe deserialization (pickle/dill/joblib/marshal loads; yaml.load without SafeLoader, and yaml.unsafe_load; torch.load without weights_only=True); command and code injection (os.system/popen, shell=True, Python eval/exec, JS eval and new Function, child_process.exec and execSync, require('child_process').exec, a bare exec( in a file that imports child_process, a Go exec.Command of a shell); SQL built from an f-string or \`%\`; tempfile.mktemp; XSS sinks (innerHTML/outerHTML assignment, document.write, dangerouslySetInnerHTML); and crypto and TLS footguns (ECB mode, createCipher without an IV on any receiver, verify=False, unverified SSL contexts, CERT_NONE, rejectUnauthorized: false, NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0, InsecureSkipVerify: true, md5/sha1 over a password). They also cover XXE parser flags and a remote \`\<script\>\` without integrity=. A separate check (_workflow_findings, agents/core/code_guidance.py:189) flags \`${{ github.event.\* }}\` inside a GitHub Actions \`run:\` step, on the run line or in its \`\|\`/\`\>\` block, whose column is the run key's own, so a \`- run: \|\` step's env:, with: and if: keys end it and are never flagged. The guards keep the usual false positives quiet: \`model.eval()\` and \`obj.eval()\`, \`def eval(\`, \`yaml.load(..., Loader=SafeLoader)\`, \`torch.load(..., weights_only=True)\`, \`regex.exec()\`, an \`===\` comparison with innerHTML, \`hashlib.md5(data)\`, a script with integrity=, whole-line comments and non-code files. Every rule is linear: a guard reads the call's balanced arguments across lines, at most MAX_CALL_CHARS (400) of them and at most MAX_CALLS_PER_LINE (8) calls a line (_call_args, agents/core/code_guidance.py:211; _guarded, agents/core/code_guidance.py:226), or the tag it matched. scan (agents/core/code_guidance.py:265) returns \`{rule, line, message}\`, at most 20 findings over the first 1 MB, with lines split at \`\\n\` only (CRLF and CR normalised), and stops after SCAN_SECONDS (0.5 s; agents/core/code_guidance.py:50); a scan cut by size or time ends with a \`scan-incomplete\` finding at the first line it did not finish, so a cut scan never reads as clean. \`.env\`, \`.env.\*\` and the shell dotfiles are scanned as shell. The findings go to five places. On the file_write approval card, FileTools.classify_mutation (agents/core/file_tools.py:1277) adds \`code_warnings\` (rule@line, at most 200 characters), \`code_warning_count\` and a title notice (\`code not fully scanned\` when a limit cut it), scanning the name as spelled and the file the write lands on (a symlink, a \`./\` or \`//\` spelling; labels, agents/core/code_guidance.py:296, names each finding once and in line order); it never sets a class, so H506's approval binding is untouched, and an instruction-file notice and the warning share the title. The gated call's \`approval_required\` answer carries \`code_warnings\`/\`code_warning_count\` (_ANSWER_LABEL_KEYS, agents/core/tool_rpc.py:200), and the tool loop's pause reply names them as warnings, not refusals (_approval_reply, agents/core/agent_runtime.py:1758): the loop ends the turn there, so the model reads them on its next turn and the owner at once. On an ungated write's result (FileTools.write_file, agents/core/file_tools.py:1024), the model reads \`code_warnings\` with a \`code_guidance\` note that they are warnings; an approved write's result lands on the approved task's record, which no model turn reads. A refused write carries none, and a failing scan never fails a write. For a marketplace install (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:858; install and install-zip answer \`code_warnings\` when there are any, agents/core/routers/skills.py:490) and a generated skill (agents/core/skills/loader.py:1211), scan_tree (agents/core/code_guidance.py:340) walks the folder, skipping symlinks; only code files count toward its 200-file bound, a file past 1 MB is read as cut, the whole walk stops after TREE_SECONDS (2 s), and the file a bound stops at gets a \`scan-incomplete\` finding. skill_propose answers the generated skill's \`code_warnings\` (agents/core/skills/tools.py:493), and generate_skill resets them first (agents/core/skills/loader.py:1051), so a skipped generation never keeps another's; the background-review and \[learn:\] generation paths only log them (their main.py is a fixed template). The owner's switch is \`security.code_guidance\` (read by enabled, agents/core/code_guidance.py:161: on by default, only an explicit off turns it off and an unreadable store keeps it on; the settings row is seeded on in settings_db DEFAULTS, and safe mode forces it back on: safe_mode.FORCED_SETTINGS, agents/core/safe_mode.py:110). An aliased child_process module (\`cp.exec\`) is not flagged. tests/test_h507_code_guidance.py (136 cases) covers every rule firing, the guard cases, the cross-language scoping, the finding shape, the table size, the workflow rule with a blank line in a block and every non-run key, the bounds, the labels, the switch, the real ToolRPC card and approved execution, a clean and a non-code write, the shared instruction notice, a failing scan, a refused write, scan_tree (symlink, bounds, switch), generation, install with the route, and the setting row. | <a id="h510"></a>H510 | Stop a web page or a rebound DNS name from driving the local API | update | Parțial | Reevaluat | The Host guard exempts _PROBE_PATHS (agents/web.py:800, applied at agents/web.py:857-858), so /healthz, /readyz and /metrics answer a rebound name: live-verified, \`Host: evil.test\` returns 200 on /healthz and /metrics and reaches the route on /readyz, while every real API route returns 400. Because DNS rebinding makes the browser treat those responses as same-origin, an attacker page still reads the full Prometheus body (route templates, request counters, latency buckets) and the /readyz body naming the configured LLM backend and the agent/channel counts. The code names this residual itself at agents/web.py:833-835 ("a rebound page can therefore still read the golden-signal counters"). Close it by narrowing the exemption rather than removing it — the operability reason for it is sound. Suggested shape: keep /healthz and /readyz exempt but strip /readyz's detail to a bare ready/not-ready when the Host is not accepted, and require an accepted Host for /metrics unless the request is unambiguously non-browser (no Origin and no Sec-Fetch-Site, or an explicit JARVIS_METRICS_ALLOW_ANY_HOST opt-in for a monitor that scrapes by an unlisted name). Needs a test alongside test_healthz_from_any_host_is_exempt asserting that a refused Host cannot read the counter body. Separately, the row's "no WebSocket variant is needed" premise is now stale: the Kanban events and Hermes runtime upgrades refuse an unaccepted Host before accepting the socket by closing it with the generic policy code 1008, not with Hermes' machine-parseable rejection reasons and close code 4403, and no pinned test drives a rebound Host against either upgrade. | <a id="h526"></a>H526 | Make a spoken reply sound like speech rather than read-out markdown | copy | Echivalent | Reevaluat | A spoken reply sounds like speech rather than read-out markdown, as Hermes requires, at every text-to-speech entry point. agents/core/voice/speech_text.py is the one normaliser (for_speech, agents/core/voice/speech_text.py:161). It drops the file-mutation verifier footer (_VERIFIER_FOOTER, agents/core/voice/speech_text.py:42), \<think\>/\<thinking\>/\<reasoning\> blocks (an unclosed one to the end, and everything before a closing tag that never opened), fenced code (\`\`\` or ~~~, an unclosed fence to the end) and HTML tags. \[text\](url) reads as its text, !\[alt\](url) as its alt, and a bare or \<autolinked\> URL as "link". Headings, list items, task boxes, block quotes and table rows lose their markers and end with a full stop (_line, agents/core/voice/speech_text.py:133); table cells read with commas; separator rows and rules are dropped. Bold, italic, strikethrough and inline-code markers go and their words stay (_inline, agents/core/voice/speech_text.py:122), with word guards so 2\*3\*4 and my_var_name survive. Symbols are said in the reply's language (_symbols, agents/core/voice/speech_text.py:113, WORDS, agents/core/voice/speech_text.py:88): & as and/și, % as percent/la sută, -\> =\> as to/spre, degrees as degrees/grade; the language comes from the request, else a ro-RO voice, else the engine default (speech_lang, agents/core/voice/speech_text.py:104). Emoji go: pictographs, flags, keycaps, skin tones, ZWJ sequences, variation selectors and tag flags (_EMOJI, agents/core/voice/speech_text.py:70). Fish \[emotion\] tags are kept intact. Newlines are flattened to one spoken line. Text with no letter or digit left is "" (_SAYABLE, agents/core/voice/speech_text.py:85), and the result is a fixed point (checked over every shared case). Verifier footer (the clause the 2026-10-10 repair closed). Only the pinned producer's exact shape is removed from speech, and only from speech: the whole warning sentence with the warning sign (with or without U+FE0F), a positive count of at most twenty digits, and a contiguous block of at least one two-space-indented bullet with text, on its own lines, LF or CRLF. Preceding and following prose is kept. Near misses stay spoken exactly as ordinary prose: a header with no bullet, an empty bullet, a count of 0, a count of twenty-one digits, no warning sign, a lone leading space, and ordinary talk about verification. The visible chat text is untouched. One limit is stated plainly: Nerva has no producer of this advisory (it appears nowhere else under agents/); the format is the donor turn finalizer's, so the strip matters for resumed foreign sessions and for model-echoed text, and this row claims nothing about a Nerva-side file-mutation verifier. Wiring. TTSEngine.speak normalises before any backend, Fish included, and synthesises nothing when nothing is left (speak, agents/core/voice/tts.py:216, normalised at agents/core/voice/tts.py:232; speech_for, agents/core/voice/tts.py:211). speak_stream normalises the whole reply before splitting sentences (agents/core/voice/tts.py:315), so a code, reasoning or footer block spanning sentences is dropped whole, and each sentence is then normalised again without change. Through TTSEngine.speak this covers the wake-word VoicePipeline, VoiceChannel.send and chat voice notes: speakable() is for_speech plus its cap (agents/core/channels/spoken_reply.py:69). POST /tts answers 204 with X-Nerva-Speech: nothing_to_say instead of synthesising (agents/core/routers/voice.py:76), and /tts/stream frames carry the spoken sentences. The HUD twin is speechText (frontend/src/speech-text.ts:110), pinned by the same shared cases as the hub. SpeechStreamFilter (frontend/src/speech-text.ts:155) drops a fenced block, a reasoning block or a footer whose markers arrive split across token deltas, holding back only a bounded tail that could still become one, and flushes cleanly. frontend/src/voice.ts uses it on the live sentence stream (frontend/src/voice.ts:297) and normalises each sentence (frontend/src/voice.ts:318); a 204 is silence, never an empty clip or the fallback voice (frontend/src/voice.ts:330). Mobile sends the reply to /tts, so the hub normalises it; ttsFetchBase64 (mobile/src/api/client.ts:2517) reads 204 as '' and speak() finishes at once (mobile/src/api/client.ts:2538, mobile/src/audio/tts.ts). Verification at this head. tests/test_h526_speech_text.py runs every shared case (57) plus the fixed-point property: 135 Python tests pass with the TTS emotion suite. frontend/src/test/speech-text.test.ts and voice-speech-text.test.tsx pass 82 tests, including a live push-to-talk turn with a fence split across deltas, a footer split at many boundaries with CRLF, the plain warning sign, and a zero or over-long count spoken exactly as the whole-reply normaliser speaks it. mobile/src/api/__tests__/tts.test.ts passes 2 under jest. Full backend suite with CI's locked dependencies and its exact command: 25,971 collected, 0 failed, 0 errors, 57 skipped here (missing optional SDKs, live Neo4j, Docker sandbox and other opt-in lanes), working tree unchanged afterwards. Full frontend suite 236 files, 2,198 tests, tsc clean. A first run with an incomplete virtualenv showed 27 failures that were missing bs4/numpy (26 reproduce identically on unmodified main); with the locked dependencies they pass. Mutation pass on the footer logic written in this repair: Python 12 mutants, 11 killed; TypeScript 10 mutants, 8 killed. The first pass left real survivors (a zero count, the twenty-digit cap, the required warning sign, and in the stream filter the plain warning sign and the same count rules); four shared cases and two stream tests now kill them. The three remaining survivors are equivalent (footer replaced with an empty string rather than a space, because the match is bounded by newlines or the string ends; a digit-after-count guard the final startsWith check already implies; \>= for === on a probe that is fed one character at a time). The earlier normaliser had its own pass (126 mutants, 124 caught, two redundant code removed). Not claimed: physical audio output or a live TTS provider. The Chromium run in the 2026-10-10 handoff used fixture STT/chat and a synthetic speech sink. | <a id="h530"></a>H530 | Not turn a silent recording into a message | copy | Echivalent | Reevaluat | Whisper nu tace când nu aude nimic — inventează. Pe liniște întoarce o propoziție fluentă din datele de antrenament: generice de subtitrare („Subtitles by the Amara.org community", „Subtitrarea: ..."), formule de încheiere („Thanks for watching!", „Mulțumesc pentru vizionare!"). Pentru o casetă de dictare e o enervare; aici e un control de siguranță, exact cum spune clauza de guvernanță a rândului: un mesaj vocal devine o tură \*inbound\*, o tură inbound poate cere lucruri, deci un transcript halucinat e o instrucțiune pe care n-a autorizat-o nimeni, intrată într-un sistem guvernat. \`hallucination.py\` o oprește. Designul e dictat de asimetria erorilor: a pierde un mesaj real e inacceptabil (cineva zice „mulțumesc" și dispare fără răspuns), a lăsa unul să treacă costă o tură ignorabilă. De aici două niveluri, nu o listă: frazele distinctive (\`CANNED\`) cad pe text; cele pe care oamenii chiar le spun (\`AMBIGUOUS\`) cad doar când durata \*decodată\* arată că înregistrarea era prea scurtă ca să le conțină — iar un apelant care nu știe durata le păstrează. Potrivirea e pe transcriptul întreg, niciodată pe substring; regula pentru generice cere marker ȘI vocabular exclusiv de generic, fiindcă prima variantă (doar markerul) mânca „am văzut pe amara.org un film bun". Filtrul rulează în \`STTEngine.transcribe\` și întoarce \`\[silence\]\` — santinela care exista deja și pe care fiecare apelant o tratează ca „nu s-a spus nimic" — deci ruta de dictare din browser o primește gratuit, nu doar calea nouă de pe Telegram. CORECTARE la auditul din 07.09: verdictul „missing" era pe jumătate greșit. A doua cerință a rândului — auto-stop pe liniște (VAD), ca utilizatorul să nu apese o tastă — EXISTĂ de mult în \`frontend/src/voice.ts\`: \`recordUtterance\` eșantionează RMS la 60 ms și oprește după \`SILENCE_MS\`, cu plafon dur și abandon când nimeni nu vorbește. Auditul a dat un \`rg -i 'vad'\` peste \`frontend/src/\` și a raportat „nimic relevant"; linia 111 spune „VAD" în litere. Ce lipsea cu adevărat era dovada: nimic nu o testa, fiindcă harness-ul comun folosește un MediaRecorder care se oprește singur și scurtcircuitează intervalul. \`voice-vad.test.tsx\` folosește unul care NU se oprește niciodată singur — dacă o tură se termină acolo, doar detectorul de liniște a putut-o termina — și acoperă fereastra de liniște, plafonul, abandonul și faptul că vorbirea continuă resetează ceasul. Named speech compatibility review: the Whisper hallucination filter and decoded-duration handling remain on the native transcribe path; named commands preserve the existing exact-sentinel behavior. Hallucination and speech selection regressions pass. [d1](../agents/core/voice/hallucination.py) [d2](../agents/core/voice/stt.py) [d3](../frontend/src/voice.ts) |

| <a id="h545"></a>H545 | Let the editor hand the agent MCP servers that exist only for that session | copy | Lipsă | Reevaluat | Every accepted part is missing: (1) an ACP session entry point (session/new, load, resume, fork) that accepts an mcpServers array; this depends on H542. (2) A session-scoped MCP registry layered over the global MCPManager, so that a server registered for one session is invisible to every other session and is torn down when the session ends. (3) Off-loop registration (asyncio.to_thread) with a bounded discovery join (default 1.5 s), so a dead server cannot block session creation. (4) A scheduled late refresh that re-reads the session's tool list after slow discovery finishes. (5) Governance: session-supplied servers pass through the same outbound MCP authorization gate as configured servers (H554, still partial), and their trust tier is capped at no wider than a configured server's.
