| <a id="h576"></a>H576 | Read a PDF / Office document / notebook as text from inside a tool call | update | Parțial | Reevaluat | Formats stop at .pdf and .docx: no .ipynb, .xlsx, .doc, .ppt, .odt, .rtf or .epub, and the text comes back plain rather than converted to Markdown. Every admitted document page still reparses the whole file, and max_bytes bounds only the text returned. The observed-size admission does not cap parser memory/CPU, decompression or full extracted-text allocation, and cannot prevent file growth after stat; bulk ingestion remains separate. Coverage measures extracted text only: nonblank but incomplete/garbled text and visual content are not detected. Only the first 16 gap ranges are listed, with an explicit omitted count; no OCR is performed. Paging is by byte offset, not a line offset/limit window. A missing parser is named (\`parser_missing\`) rather than installed lazily. Independent #1233 remaining limits: Formats stop at .pdf and .docx: no .ipynb, .xlsx, .doc, .ppt, .odt, .rtf or .epub, and the text comes back plain rather than converted to Markdown. There is no size refusal for documents (Hermes refuses over 50 MB): the whole file is parsed again on every page request, and max_bytes bounds only the text returned. There is no scanned-page coverage warning naming the page ranges that yielded no text, which the row calls the clever half. Paging is by byte offset, not a line offset/limit window. | <a id="h579"></a>H579 | Pull a file or slice of a file into a message inline (@ context references) | copy | Echivalent | Reevaluat | The owner's own chat attaches @file:path, @file:path#L10-40 and @file:"a b.md" for the turn. agents/core/context_refs.py holds the rules. expand (agents/core/context_refs.py:209) finds a reference that starts a word or follows an opening bracket, quote or backtick, and not one inside a word or a path (x@file:, a/@file:, @@file:) (_REF_RE, agents/core/context_refs.py:49); a double-quoted path may hold spaces, #L7 is one line and #L2-L3 a range, and trailing punctuation or a closing quote is not part of it. The routes keep the owner's message as typed: commands, skills, LLM-backend control, the router and memory see only it. The "--- Attached Context ---" section is bound to the turn (bind_attached, agents/core/context_refs.py:251; agents/web.py:1317 on /chat, and inside the stream task at agents/web.py:1415) and appended after the message only in the model prompt (attached_block, agents/core/context_refs.py:266; Orchestrator._build_agent_turn_text, agents/core/orchestrator.py:3850), so the file text is never stored as the owner's words, replayed in a later turn's history or embedded. Hermes keeps the expanded message in the user turn; Nerva shows the attachment to the model for the attaching (tainted) turn only. Each file's text is in a fence longer than any backtick run in it, so no line of it can close the fence (_fence, agents/core/context_refs.py:194), under a header that names the file as typed and the lines actually attached, \`(line 7)\` or \`(lines 2-3)\`, as attached file content, not instructions; injection patterns and a forged Attached Context marker are flagged in that header (\`flagged: …\`, _flags, agents/core/context_refs.py:180), not withheld. Each path is resolved through the same FileScope as file_read (_attach_one, agents/core/context_refs.py:133), so outside the file roots, .. traversal, a symlink escape and a secret-looking path such as .env are refused. A missing file, a directory, a binary file (a NUL in its first 8 KB), a bad line range, a range past the end, an unreadable file, an over-long name, a denied stat and an unknown ~user each become a one-line warning in the same section instead of failing the message. With JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS unset, the file tools' default root \<data home\>/workspace is used; only an unusable JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS makes the section say nothing was attached. The limits are 8 distinct references per message, 64 KB per reference and 128 KB in all, counted in bytes. A cut reference says so, and a repeated one is attached once. A line range skips the lines before it a 64K-character chunk at a time, up to 64M characters into the file (MAX_SCAN_CHARS; past it, the warning "line N is too far into the file"), keeps at most the byte budget and never reads a line whole (_read_lines, agents/core/context_refs.py:105); invalid UTF-8 is read with replacement characters. The expansion runs on /chat and /chat/stream (agents/web.py:1306, agents/web.py:1534), off the event loop, so both the HUD and nerva chat get it; the one message that skips it is a raw checkpoint command (\`/rollback\` or \`/checkpoints\` as the whole message, checkpoint_command_name), which never becomes a model turn, so nothing is read, bound or tainted for it. It never runs for a channel message, as Hermes' gateway does not expand either. A turn that attached anything is tainted: handle_input and handle_input_stream call _taint_attached_context (agents/core/orchestrator.py:378, :2372, :2593), which raises the turn's action origin to recall:untrusted. An action planned from attached content therefore escalates GRANT to QUEUE at the kernel, while an inbound turn keeps its more specific origin. complete (agents/core/context_refs.py:272) lists in-scope completions for what follows @file:, with directories ending in / and a path with a space quoted (a name no reference could name is left out). It shows dot files only when asked and never secret paths or links out of the roots, is bounded to 50 entries, and returns nothing for a prefix over 1,024 characters. GET /api/context-refs (agents/core/routers/commands.py:63, user-guarded, read-only) serves it and the reference types, and answers 503 file_roots_unusable when the roots cannot be used. The HUD composer (frontend/src/cockpit.tsx:229, :284, frontend/src/context-refs.tsx) offers the reference types while \`@\` or \`@fi\` is typed (Tab takes \`@file:\`), then the in-scope paths; a list is shown only for the text it was fetched for. tests/test_h579_context_refs.py (70 cases) covers the bounds, parsing, whole files, line ranges (single, L-form, past the end), every refusal and warning, a symlink, punctuation, word starts, dedupe, the byte cut, the shared budget, the reference limit, an unreadable file, invalid UTF-8, the roots, an explicit scope and the marker; completion (prefixes, dot files, secrets, roots, a long prefix, a file or missing folder, the bound); both routes, the completion route, the turn taint on both paths, and an inbound turn. The review round added attached text never read as the owner's command (a slash command, a skill, a backend switch) and never stored or carried to a later turn, through the real routes; a file that cannot close its fence; injection and a forged marker flagged; a range in one huge line bounded in memory and a range of many short lines linear; a range too far into a file; quoted paths and their completion; references after brackets and quotes and not inside words; the distinct-reference limit; the header's path and lines; paths the system refuses to look at; and the roots. frontend/src/test/context-refs.test.tsx has 6 cases. The row's 53 mutants predate this code; the review round's 34: 28 caught at once, five after five cases were added, and one equivalent (a kept read stops at the budget either way, since readline(0) answers ""). Local auxiliary diff review (2026-10-02,aa4865b5): the claimed behavior is outside the four changed producer methods. Parent AST comparison and re-read source/citations confirm unchanged mechanisms; the cited backend test modules pass in the frozen full run. Existing frontend evidence remains tied to unchanged source. No new capability or mutation claim is added. Re-review on 2026-10-02: InputBar now passes its active agent into the image hook; inline file-reference completion and insertion remain unchanged. Existing no-media memory, text turns, previous composer route, and unrelated orchestrator/HUD behavior retain their prior branches; focused H277/H513/composer/session tests, 1,872 frontend tests, TypeScript and HUD build pass. Existing verdict preserved; this note does not claim live-provider acceptance or a new Hermes capability. Collateral active-image review (2026-10-03, a30603e0): cockpit submit readiness changed only for explicit image selections and orchestrator added a referenced-image provenance marker. The @file context reference parser, completion and insertion branches are unchanged at their pinned citations; the existing equivalent verdict is preserved. Collateral actuation review (2026-10-03, Task3 working tree): The orchestrator edit is limited to the post-answer approval-observation acknowledgment. Attached-file expansion, taint and prompt insertion retain their cited paths. Existing equivalent verdict and remaining limits are preserved; this is source review, not live-provider evidence. Collateral review (2026-10-03, fresh owner authority): @file parsing, taint insertion and prompt attachment still use unchanged branches. The owner-principal edit changes who is an admin in Telegram, not the web-only attachment path or its bounds. The prior equivalent verdict is retained from claim-specific source review; this is no new parity or live acceptance claim. Re-read (2026-10-11, PR #1249 head f9e130b5): agents/web.py now skips the expansion (and the notes prefix) for a raw checkpoint command, which never reaches the model; every other message still expands on both routes, is bound to the turn and reset after it. The orchestrator and cockpit drift moved the cited lines without touching the taint, the attached block or the composer's completion. The test file's hub fixture now binds a native checkpoint session (the routes' owner guard) and the off-the-event-loop test observes the expander's thread through the real /chat and /chat/stream functions instead of reading their source; still 70 cases, all passing, with the 6 frontend cases. settings_db.py is no longer pinned: no claim of this row lives there. Each draft is first reviewed against the server (prepare / selected-prepare with image digests, destination binding, data-policy and remote/training/cost acknowledgements), and App.submit sends an image draft to runVision (frontend/src/app.tsx:511, frontend/src/app.tsx:477). runVision picks one of three routes (frontend/src/vision-turn.ts:8): POST /api/vlm/composer/describe-prepared (agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:499), POST /api/vlm/composer/chat-prepared for a selected main route (agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:584) or POST /api/vlm/composer/selected-chat for a selected Ollama route (agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:1092); the router is registered at agents/web.py:1669. All three routes check data-URI signatures and bound raster decoding (validate_raster, agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:61) and refuse a malformed body with its first reason instead of FastAPI's echoing 422 (_BoundedValidationRoute, agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:28). describe-prepared and chat-prepared also refuse a non-local destination without the owner's acknowledgement (agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:718) and call VLMBackend.generate_vision_checked (agents/core/llm/vlm.py:460); selected-chat is local Ollama only, refusing any remote acknowledgement (agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:985-987) and streaming /api/chat itself (agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:1051); the H277 native adapters (OpenRouter, DeepInfra, Nous, Claude, Gemini, Responses, xAI), empty-reply recovery and reply normalization sit behind that guard. The terminal: \`nerva chat --image PATH\` (repeatable, up to eight) and \`--clipboard-image\` (agents/cli/nerva.py:445-448) turn the chat verb into a vision turn (dispatch at agents/cli/nerva.py:2748, _vision_turn at agents/cli/nerva.py:3119) that refuses --agent/--session/--reasoning and never posts to /chat. Files are typed by signature (_image_mime, agents/cli/nerva.py:2862; _read_image, agents/cli/nerva.py:2872); the clipboard is read by wl-paste, xclip, pngpaste/osascript or PowerShell (_clipboard_command, agents/cli/nerva.py:2947; _clipboard_image, agents/cli/nerva.py:3057) under a bounded, deadline-killed reader (_run_reader, agents/cli/nerva.py:2972), and an off-machine destination needs --remote-vision naming it (agents/cli/nerva.py:3208). Governance gap found on this re-read: the previous verdict rested on isolation (the vision answer a client-only transcript entry, ordinary turns posting only {message, agent} to /chat/stream). Since #1233/#1246 that holds only for describe-prepared and the terminal. The chat-prepared and selected-chat routes commit the image-derived question/answer pair into the durable conversation (orch.complete_selected_image_turn at agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:619-623 and agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:1065), and later text turns in that session post to /chat/stream with the session_id (frontend/src/app.tsx:404-405) and read that history. That history is now governed (H586 fix, 2026-10-12, c9f67240, 0631eeb9, 9a485766, 44b53b51, 0bc59ec5 and 307b33eb): every later chat turn runs _guard_media_history (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2359-2377) at both turn entries (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2453 and agents/core/orchestrator.py:2674), which reads the session history and, when any turn carries media, raises the turn's action origin through mark_turn_recall_tainted, so a side-effecting action derived from that history is queued for approval (ASK) instead of auto-granted, and an unreadable history marks the turn too; one-shot completions (process/process_detailed: the autonomy _llm executor, nightly reflection, the summarize route) run the same guard inside an action-origin binding scoped to the call (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2224-2226), so the mark never leaks to the caller; image turns are embedded with taint metadata (taint_source external:image, agents/core/memory/manager.py:342-345), so recalling the image reading in any later turn taints that turn through the existing RAG guard, and a session_search hit on a turn carrying media is flagged image_derived and taints the turn too (agents/core/memory/session_search.py:239-240 and agents/core/memory/session_search.py:244-248), and, since the model's call runs search_sessions in a worker thread whose own mark cannot reach the turn, the production mechanism is the registered tool handler declaring tainted on its result (agents/core/memory/session_search.py:281-283), which the agent tool loop reads as declared_taint and turns into the turn's mark; and a session holding a media turn is never promoted to durable memory, like a foreign import: _session_has_media (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2379-2384) stops the per-turn learning review (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3978 and agents/core/orchestrator.py:4064), the LivingMemory feed (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4093) /refine, which answers image_history_not_promotable (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4023-4024), and nightly reflection, whose KG/core-lesson consolidation skips a window holding a committed image turn (agents/core/autonomy/reflection.py:166-167); /undo, on the web (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1961-1963) and on channels (agents/core/channels/session_lifecycle.py:226-228), copies the kept turns with their media provenance, so an undo cannot launder the image reading into trusted history. tests/test_h586_image_history_taint.py pins the QUEUE verdict through the real kernel authorize (with a stubbed history and with a real MemoryManager after a committed image turn), the untouched text-only origin, the fail-safe mark, both entries' call order, a one-shot completion over image history running tainted without leaking the mark, the tainted embedding read back through rag_guard, and the refusals of review, LivingMemory and /refine, a web /undo keeping the provenance (guard, promotion gate and tainted re-embedding) and nightly reflection skipping the image window and a session_search hit on an image reading tainting the turn, directly and through ToolRPCServer.handle (13 cases, red before the change). Stated limits: the guard reads the held history, which keeps the newest 100 turns, so a media turn that has aged out of it no longer marks later turns (its embedding stays tainted), and with the opt-in memory.compression_summarizer the per-session summary cache can carry image-derived text past that window. Tests this session: 25 pinned backend files (tests/test_h277_image_turn_memory.py, tests/test_composer_vision.py, tests/test_nerva_chat_image.py, tests/test_h586b_image_review.py, tests/test_h586c_image_review.py, tests/test_h586_image_history_taint.py and the 19 pinned tests/test_h277_\* files) 509 passed, 0 failed; frontend/src/test/composer-images.test.tsx and frontend/src/test/composer-vision-turn.test.tsx 50 passed; frontend/e2e/composer-images.spec.ts (Playwright) and mobile were not run. Known limits kept: the receipt's model stays null for a terminal image turn; no live-provider or native-mobile acceptance. | <a id="h594"></a>H594 | Have the agent pick up a project's conventions automatically (context files) | copy | Echivalent | Reevaluat | Nerva reads a project's convention files into the turn, as Hermes reads its context files and subdirectory hints. agents/core/project_context.py walks from the nearest git root (never above the file root) down to the working directory (llm.project_dir when it is a folder inside the roots, H218; else the first JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS root; since #1233 a bound kanban workspace's cwd instead, read inside that workspace's scope), and reads AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules and .cursor/rules/\*.mdc in each directory in that order (CONVENTION_NAMES, agents/core/project_context.py:59; candidates, agents/core/project_context.py:168). A directory that the model's file_read, file_list or file_search touches is noted for the session (note_tool_path, agents/core/project_context.py:408, bounded to 8 directories and 256 sessions, agents/core/project_context.py:70-71); its chain is read on every later turn, and the tool's own result carries the files the turn had not seen yet, marked tainted so the loop fences it (attach, agents/core/project_context.py:427; _with_project_context, agents/core/file_tools.py:653, called by the three read tools at agents/core/file_tools.py:841, agents/core/file_tools.py:897 and agents/core/file_tools.py:1020). A script's file call (execute_code, no tool turn) brings none. A local terminal_run runs only after approval, by the worker from the queue: the queuing turn's session is recorded at intake (note_task, agents/core/project_context.py:439) — on ToolRPCServer.handle's generic gated path (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:638) and, since #1233 gave terminal_run its own trusted intake, in _terminal_intake (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1192, the call at agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1257; registered with gated_intake and gated_review at agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1284-1285) — and when the approved command ran locally, note_terminal (agents/core/project_context.py:451; keyed by the task id, not by a turn) notes its cwd for that session, so its next turn reads the chain (_rpc_terminal_run, agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1189). Normally the command runs outside any turn and its result goes to the task row, not to the model; with Smart review or a live owner-once/consent reply, the registrar's gated_review (review_terminal_task, agents/core/autonomy/terminal_review.py:22-24) awaits the worker's own run of that task and hands the queue-verified result back to the model in the same turn — the directory is noted either way. A project SOUL.md, HEARTBEAT.md or IDENTITY.md is never read, not even through a symlink (HUB_FILES, agents/core/project_context.py:63; _admit, agents/core/project_context.py:183). Every file is resolved through FileScope (outside the roots, symlink escape and secret paths refused), must be a regular file (a FIFO is never opened), and is bounded to 20 KB, with 40 KB and 12 files a turn and 8 rules a directory (agents/core/project_context.py:65-68), shared by parallel tool calls under the turn's lock; a cut says how much was shown, a file past the budget is named, and files past a count cap are counted (load_file, agents/core/project_context.py:220; collect, agents/core/project_context.py:239; render, agents/core/project_context.py:274). Each file's text and name are scanned with detect_injection_normalized, plus Unicode TAG characters (decoded and scanned) and the fence's markers (_detect, agents/core/project_context.py:122). A flagged file becomes a \[BLOCKED ...\] line naming the rules (injection_flag_names) with none of its text, and a flagged name is withheld; other names have non-printable characters escaped and undecodable bytes replaced. The caveated block, which holds the files in the untrusted-data fence, sits after the core-memory block in _build_agent_turn_text (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3866-3872); _begin_project_context (agents/core/orchestrator.py:388-416) builds it off the event loop at turn start in both turn paths (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2470 and agents/core/orchestrator.py:2699) and marks the turn recall-tainted when any file was given, so an action planned from it escalates GRANT to QUEUE. A noted directory's files are in every later turn of the session, so those turns are tainted too: web_search, web_extract and memory writes refuse until the setting is off or the hub restarts. A guest's turn is given none of them. It is off with llm.project_context_files (agents/core/project_context.py:74) and in safe mode (layer project_context, agents/core/safe_mode.py:77, named on the HUD banner; enabled, agents/core/project_context.py:312). tests/test_h594_project_context.py: 66 cases. The terminal intake still calls note_task, and the approved terminal handler still calls note_terminal with the actual cwd/result; the new signed owner-once continuation reaches that same handler only after a live owner reply and private worker claim. The source/guest taint and admission rules remain. The prior equivalent code verdict remains supported as code behavior, without claiming a live project run. | <a id="h670"></a>H670 | The default identity prompt is a behavior contract, and it lives in one file | update | Echivalent | Reevaluat | The shared identity band exists. agents/_identity/IDENTITY.md is one behaviour contract: the reply-sizing rule (match length to the weight of the ask), earned depth, the named prohibitions (no filler, no restating the request, no re-summarizing, no narrating visible tool calls), the anti-sycophancy line ('agree because it is right, not because the owner said it') and 'say when you do not know'. Its reply rules govern the agent's own replies to the owner: text drafted in someone else's voice (an email, a post, a message written as the owner) keeps that voice, greetings and sign-offs included, and a persona's warmth or curiosity lives inside the answer (review-H670 m-5); its honesty rules hold for everything an agent writes, drafted text included (review-H670b m-1). Its leading maintainer note (stripped before the model sees it, _strip_maintainer_note, agents/core/agent.py:453) says never to add 'be targeted and efficient in your exploration', and why. The repo-root SOUL.md mirrors the text, so agents working on the repo read the contract the product ships; a test keeps the two equal. identity_path (agents/core/agent.py:438) resolves it as soul_path_for does a persona: the data home's souls/IDENTITY.local.md, then a gitignored agents/_identity/IDENTITY.local.md, then the shipped file. read_identity (agents/core/agent.py:481) runs it through the same H387 helpers as a SOUL (the injection scan on the uncapped body, then the cap), announces a flagged or truncated contract (its blocked and quarantined stubs name the contract, not a persona), caps it at its own 4,000 characters (IDENTITY_MAX_CHARS, never above the persona's cap, so the two bands stay within the persona cap plus 4,000), and reads it once per settled file signature for the whole process. An override that cannot be read (not UTF-8, a directory, no permission) is reported at ERROR and the shipped contract used instead, cached against the shipped file's signature so an edit of it is seen; a contract that cannot be located or read at all leaves the agent without it; none of these stops an agent from being built. Agent.system_prompt (agents/core/agent.py:572) is the contract, then the agent's persona (either may be empty; an agent without a SOUL still gets the contract). Every place a system prompt is built uses it: Agent.process (agents/core/agent.py:1090) and the synthesis path in agent.py, and the orchestrator's two sites (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2824, agents/core/orchestrator.py:4685) through _system_prompt_of (agents/core/orchestrator.py:512). | <a id="h672"></a>H672 | A never-ending session picks up config, skill and tool changes at the compaction boundary | copy | Parțial | Reevaluat | \*\*The boundaries are opt-in, so on a shipped default nothing migrates\*\*: the conversation-level commit exists only with \`memory.context_compression\` on (default off) and the in-turn fold only with \`llm.tool_loop_enabled\` on (default off) — a default install still needs a restart for a persona edit, exactly as before. \*\*Execution-admission scope:\*\* production coordinator-wired agent-loop calls now recheck live profile authorization before preflight/intake, including between folds. This does not cancel an already-running tool or rewrite queued approvals; direct/script RPC and approved task execution retain their existing contracts. A standalone runtime wired only with \`tool_profile\` must explicitly supply the separate \`execution_profile\` hook to gain this check. The model's offered schemas and gate/taint views still refresh only at their existing boundaries. \*\*The persona migration is process-wide\*\*: \`orchestrator.agents\` is every agent and \`agent.soul\` is the one dict every session's system prompt reads, so the session that commits migrates the persona for all sessions (the boundary log line says so); refreshing only the routed agents would need the route at \`_history_for_prompt\`, which it does not have. \*\*On the staged shared-route path the turn's budget is computed against the persona in force before the commit\*\* (\`_shared_route_plan\` → \`build()\` measures \`agent.soul\` while planning; the refresh runs in \`accept()\` → \`publish()\`), so a persona that grew is sent that turn with a budget computed for the old size — bounded by \`_soul_max_chars\`, self-correcting next turn; the H363 cached prefix and the H673 usage anchor under-count for one turn after a rebuild the same way. The probe trusts the kernel's signature; what the builder reads outside the file (the scan patterns) is code and needs a restart. The prompt half covers the SOUL only: Nerva's plugin and skills sections live in the user prompt and were already per-turn, so there is no plugin section in the system prompt to fail open — the fail-open is exercised on the SOUL builder. The in-turn boundary does not rebuild \`messages\[0\]\`: a persona change reaches the \*next\* turn, not the loop in flight. "A newly configured MCP server appears without a restart" is only as true as the MCP manager's registration into ToolRPC is hot, which this slice did not verify. The lineage row stays at \`nerva.context-compaction.v1\`; the boundary note is a log line plus the runtime event, not a field on the row. \`refresh_tools\` compares names, so a tool whose schema changed under the same name is adopted only because the fresh list is taken whenever the set moved, never on its own. The stale comment at \`agents/core/file_tools.py\` saying \`_load_soul\` runs no injection scan predates H387 and is left for a hygiene commit (it would drift five unrelated rows). Nine ledger rows cite \`agent.py\`, \`agent_runtime.py\` or \`orchestrator.py\` and were drifted by this branch (and by #1188 on main: its registry path in \`orchestrator.py\`, and the pairing kwarg, refusal branch and lifespan hand-over in \`telegram.py\` and \`web.py\`, which H146, H449, H364 and H671 also cite and were read against — the pairing store is not their subject); each was re-read against the diff on its cited paths before its hashes moved. Six keep their text and take fresh stamps — H146, H298, H363, H364, H449, H679: the in-turn re-resolution runs through \`_profiled\`, which still applies the job toolset on both sides of the profile, and the result-spill, cache, reasoning and job-pin mechanism those rows cite is untouched. Three are rewritten — H387: the ERROR line now comes from \`_announce_soul_verdict\` behind the \`_read_soul\` builder, for boot and boundary alike; H671 and H673: \`publish()\` re-reads the personas after the clock CAS, and the staged-route budget limit above is now on H673's own row. The 16 other needs_review rows on main (H060, H061, H068, H071, H104, H108, H130, H135, H139, H398, H477, H510, H523, H683 from #1188's edits to \`orchestrator.py\`, \`web.py\` and \`telegram.py\`; H288 and H684 from #1187's \`heartbeat.py\` and \`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md\`) are main's own drift, not this branch's, and are left untouched here; #1187's five-line comment in \`orchestrator.py\` re-drifted the nine rows above once more, and they were re-read against it and re-stamped. | <a id="h674"></a>H674 | Compression cannot stall the user: bounded holds, inactivity deadlines and derived thresholds | update | Echivalent | Reevaluat | A compaction summary no longer holds the owner's turn past a short bound, and a silent summarizer is cut. Hermes keeps two clocks: how long the summary may make the user wait, and how long the summarizer may go quiet. Nerva awaited the strict-local summarizer inline with neither. Its only limit was the httpx read timeout (120 s for Ollama), a total-duration wait on a non-streaming call, and nothing told the owner. (1) Bounded hold. ContextCompressor takes a gate (agents/core/context_compressor.py:327, used at :605). The orchestrator builds it per turn (_summary_gate, agents/core/orchestrator.py:4383, passed at :4514) around SummaryHold (agents/core/compaction_hold.py:149). SummaryHold.wait (:159) waits at most memory.compression_max_turn_hold_seconds for the LLM summary (settings_db.py:312; default 10 s, 0 = never wait, clamped 0..120 by hold_seconds, compaction_hold.py:64). One summary per session is written at a time: a turn that finds one still in flight neither waits on it again nor starts a second. Past the hold the turn goes on without the summary, and compress marks the result summary_deferred (context_compressor.py:630). compact (:422) then sends the turns verbatim, their old images dropped, when they still fit the window under the owner's memory.compression_max_tokens; otherwise it sends the deterministic digest. The summary keeps being written. When it lands it seeds this session's iterative-merge prior (_ctx_summary_cache), but only if no newer turn has replaced the prior this turn started from, and never through the compaction-clock CAS: publish commits only what the prompt was built from, and never writes the digest over the pending summary (orchestrator.py:4616). A turn cancelled while it waits (Stop, a client gone) still leaves its summary for the next turn. A summary that fails later seeds nothing and is logged by name. aclose stops what is still being written within the task budget (orchestrator.py:5351; SummaryHold.aclose, compaction_hold.py:198). (2) The owner is told. record_turn_notice (agents/core/turn_notices.py:35; a per-turn sink collected like turn_approvals, one notice per code) carries DEFERRED_NOTICE (compaction_hold.py:39) out as notices on /chat (ChatResponse.notices, agents/web.py:1143, TurnNotice :1118) and on every /chat/stream end event, the failed one included (:1490, :1497). The HUD shows each notice as a system line under the reply (frontend/src/turn-notices.ts, app.tsx:442). The hub log says the summary was deferred and, later, that it landed. (3) Inactivity deadline. The summarizer now streams (stream_summary, compaction_hold.py:89, called at agents/core/llm/auxiliary_text.py:148). It is cut after memory.compression_summary_idle_seconds with nothing received (settings_db.py:313; default 60 s, up to 600, no "off": idle_seconds, compaction_hold.py:72). Any chunk counts as life: a visible token, and a reasoning chunk that shows no text, through the new on_activity callback on the Ollama and LM Studio streams (agents/core/llm/base.py:737, :1022). A slow stream that keeps talking is never cut. A cut stream is cancelled and given CLOSE_GRACE (1 s) to close its HTTP response. A backend with no stream is awaited whole. A degraded reply ("⚠️ …", "\[backend error …\]") or an empty one is now a failure, and so the digest is used. Before, the non-streaming generate could hand an error text over as the summary. It also covers the notice on /chat and every stream end event, the collector unbound after /chat, and on_activity on both local streams. frontend src/test/turn-notices.test.ts covers the HUD. 72 mutants: 70 caught after nine survivors got cases. | <a id="h677"></a>H677 | Boot warm-up before accepting work, and every shutdown wait has a short explicit budget | update | Echivalent | Reevaluat | The bounded warm-up gate, status reporting, per-step shutdown budgets and ChatLanes ordering/8-turn concurrency retain their existing implementations. Ordinary Telegram batched turns, generic callbacks, group observations and rejection reasons enter the chat lane. Reserved current aut1 callbacks have a separate post-flush reply lane; reserved autc callbacks intercept before flush, and only registered current offers use their independent bounded32-task lane. Stale or malformed autc callbacks refuse promptly outside the ordinary lane. Stop revokes both registries, cancels every reserved fast-task set (five since the pending-input lane landed) and waits on their combined set for at most LANE_DRAIN_BUDGET before ordinary lane drain. Offline lifecycle/owner/consent regressions preserve the accepted boot/shutdown verdict; this does not establish live shutdown or renew older mutation receipts. Batch collateral review (2026-10-04, base9bfa085c): Native reusable-consent \`/deny\` joins aut1/autc as a reserved fast-lane exception: original direct replies to current delivered cards use a bounded private task set; stop cancels and drains it. Ordinary ChatLanes ordering, warm-up, status and shutdown budgets remain unchanged. This does not prove live Telegram shutdown. Owner-once denial collateral review (2026-10-04, base 22005244): Telegram now has a fourth bounded fast-task set for native owner-once \`/deny\` replies. \`stop\` revokes both registries, cancels and waits on the union of owner-once callbacks, owner-once denials, reusable-consent callbacks and reusable-consent denials before the ordinary lane drain (agents/core/channels/telegram.py:379-404). The existing warm-up, status, per-step budget and ChatLanes ordering/concurrency code is unchanged. The owner-once offline test exercises the occupied-lane dispatch; the four-set shutdown claim was from direct source review, not a fresh live shutdown or mutation proof. Re-read (2026-10-11, base f9e130b5, PR #1249): the drift since the pins is the pending-input (H067) Telegram transport and forum-topic replies; no lifecycle claim regressed. \`stop\` now cancels five reserved fast-task sets (owner-once callbacks, owner-once denials, reusable-consent callbacks, reusable-consent denials and pending-input \`h067:\` callbacks) and waits on their union for at most LANE_DRAIN_BUDGET (agents/core/channels/telegram.py:396-404), then drains the ordinary lanes and closes the ephemeral system-notice deletes within the same budget (agents/core/channels/telegram.py:421-425). \`h067:\` callbacks are intercepted ahead of the consent parsing into their own bounded 32-task set and answer 'Not applied.' when the set is full or the transport is stopped (agents/core/channels/telegram.py:883-898). Fresh, directly authored, un-forwarded text that answers a delivered clarification may be consumed by the pending-reply handler before batching and the chat lane (agents/core/channels/telegram.py:1047-1050); that handler is awaited inline in the poll loop and only a \`True\` result skips the ordinary path (agents/core/channels/telegram.py:1071-1080); its gateway and orchestrator halves are documented as pending-only ingress with no model fallback (read, not pinned). The stop-cancel of the fifth set is exercised offline (tests/test_pending_input_native_transport.py:303-322) and the Telegram lane drain stays within budget (tests/test_h677_boot_and_shutdown.py:756-770). The warm-up gate waits at most the configured budget and opens either way (agents/core/lifecycle_budget.py:102-119); the lifespan still runs it between load_agents and start_channels (tests/test_h677_boot_and_shutdown.py:165-171); /api/status and /readyz still report it (agents/core/routers/status.py:119-120; agents/core/routers/ops.py:142-143); every channel stop is bounded by CHANNEL_STOP_BUDGET (agents/core/channels/manager.py:121-127) and the orchestrator's teardown waits stay bounded in the source (tests/test_h677_boot_and_shutdown.py:481-489); lanes still run 8 turns at once (agents/core/channels/chat_lanes.py:21) and drain within a budget (agents/core/channels/chat_lanes.py:66-78). Drift notes outside the pins: the orchestrator's new stop_channels waits (session-lifecycle stall-watcher close, 2 s default; embeddings flush, 5 s) and the lifespan's new Hermes-runtime stop (process STOP_TIMEOUT 7 s then kill, websocket close_timeout 3 s, bridge thread join 2 s; a no-op unless that runtime was started) are internally bounded, though the latter is not wrapped in bounded(). agents/web.py, agents/core/orchestrator.py and agents/core/settings_db.py are no longer pinned: their H677 code is unchanged and the lifespan-ordering, source-scan and setting-declaration tests carry those claims. Offline verdict (165 + 32 tests passed on this base); not a live shutdown proof. | <a id="h683"></a>H683 | Chat replies stream, can be edited or deleted, and acknowledge receipt at ingest | update | Parțial | Reevaluat | (1) No edit or delete in the base contract: ChannelAdapter (agents/core/channels/base.py:14) still declares only abstract start/stop/send plus receive, and no adapter implements a delete operation for a sent reply (the only deleteMessage in agents/ is Telegram's TTL cleanup of ephemeral system notices at telegram.py:504, not a channel-contract method), so a sealed streamed preview cannot be removed and there is no base method that fails loudly for a channel that cannot edit; the fallback to a whole reply is silent. (2) Slack and Discord do not stream: both descriptors declare supports_edit=True (agents/core/channels/slack.py:105, agents/core/channels/discord.py:51) but neither adapter implements begin_stream or an edit call (Slack's send posts via chat_postMessage only, slack.py:609), and _begin_channel_draft refuses both (and ntfy) because a streamed draft would publish tokens before the channel.reply approval; streaming there needs an approval contract that covers output not yet generated. (3) No acknowledgement at ingest: Telegram sends a typing chat action only while reading an inbound attachment (telegram.py:1632) and a record_voice action before a spoken reply, so an ordinary text message gets no receipt signal until the first streamed token or the whole reply; Slack and Discord send none (the Slack Socket Mode envelope ack is a transport ack to Slack, not a signal the sender sees). The exact frozen clause requires configured-path availability, not unsupported model workspace context or wider job options. Native scripts root and approved script-only workdir are the accepted mapping. Broader options and production-host observation remain independently open. Current disjoint provider token categories require an explicit denominator; the historic 1000 input plus 800 cached equals 80% example is not a valid disjoint-counter formula. Render only selected available fields, including the 70/40 cache thresholds when that metric exists; model/background-task/duration vocabulary entries are reserved but not implemented by this latency slice. Independent #1233 remaining limits: (1) Compute a per-turn readout: wall latency; output tokens/sec over generation time; context % of the resolved model window; compressions count; and cache hit as a delta since the last cache-invalidating event (model switch or accepted compaction), omitted when there were zero cache reads. Attach it to the /chat/stream end event and the /chat response, leaving fields absent when there is no data. (2) Add a display.status_bar_fields setting with a fixed field vocabulary shared by backend and HUD. (3) Add a HUD status strip on the chat surface that renders only the selected fields, hides omitted ones and colours cache hit at the 70/40 thresholds. (4) Backend and frontend tests. | <a id="h687"></a>H687 | A recurring instruction runs once immediately, then on its cadence | update | Echivalent | Reevaluat | Built on this branch and reworked after two reviews. A recurring instruction now runs once when it is created, then on its cadence, with Hermes' split kept: - Hermes' /loop is an interval. LoopManager.set() starts it with next_due_at=now (hermes_cli/loops.py:466), and the reply says the first wakeup fires now. - A Hermes cron job waits for its first computed run. Nerva applies the /loop behaviour to its cron-style jobs where the schedule is an interval. Before this change, a new Nerva job always waited for its first slot, and every confirmation named only the schedule. Every creation surface goes through JobRunner.arm (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:1575): - POST /api/jobs (agents/core/routers/jobs.py:142); - the /remind slash command (agents/core/commands.py:304); - \`nerva jobs create\`, which posts to that route and prints the hub's confirmation (tests/test_nerva_cli.py:1274); - the HUD arm and JobCreateDialog notes (armNote, frontend/src/panels/jobs.tsx:38, used at frontend/src/panels/jobs.tsx:157 and frontend/src/panels/jobs.tsx:163). JobRunner.create is a thin wrapper around it (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:1573). first_run_policy (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:561) decides what runs before its first slot. Only an agent-instruction job does (ask, brief or task, or a script or monitor source), and only on an interval cadence. is_interval_cron (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:535) reads what the cron fires on, not how it is written: every hour with one minute or the minutes of a \`\*/N\`, or one minute in the hours of a \`\*/N\`, with no weekday, day or month restriction. So '0 0-23/2' and '0 0,12' count as '0 \*/2' and '0 \*/12', while two times of day ('0 9,21') and '\*/5 \*/2' (only in even hours) are calendar schedules. These wait for their first slot: - a calendar schedule (a 07:00 morning brief armed in the evening, a weekday job armed on Saturday); - a reminder; - a repeat-limited job, whose early run would spend one of its few attempts (critic note 15); - anything during quiet hours, whose output would be held and delivered after the next fresh run's; - anything whose first slot is near (first_run_margin, agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:556): nearer than two minutes or than a quarter of the cadence (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:503-504), read from the real cron in the app's schedule timezone, the zone the job's trigger is registered with (slot_timing, agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:1610; tests/test_job_first_run.py:520 sets the host scheduler to another zone to prove that one is not read). "every 12 hours" armed 45 minutes before its noon slot waits for it instead of running twice within the hour. first_run_decision (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:598) applies it at creation. A paused or disabled job never fires, and the create call's \`first_run\` (StrictBool, agents/core/routers/jobs.py:34; \`--first-run/--no-first-run\`, tests/test_job_first_run.py:363) overrides the policy either way. It is a creation-time choice, never a stored option: validate_options refuses it, so PATCH cannot store it and no rollback trips on it. The first run is a dispatch request drained by _fire_once (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:1723) under the shared job gate (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:1600; ORIGINS and the column at agents/core/autonomy/jobs_dispatch.py:12 and agents/core/autonomy/jobs_dispatch.py:40). Its origin is 'first_run' when the policy chose it and 'first_run_asked' when the create call asked for it. - The request is durable, so the drain checks a policy first run against first_run_policy again when it comes to run (first_run_due, agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:1626; agents/core/autonomy/jobs_dispatch.py:214). By then the job may have been edited into a calendar schedule, a reminder or a repeat-limited job, quiet hours may have begun, or a scheduler that was down may have left its first slot near. The request is then cancelled and names the reason. An asked first run is not second-guessed. - The drain runs both with force=False (agents/core/autonomy/jobs_dispatch.py:223), so _fire_once applies the pause check (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:1737), the emergency stop (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:1743), option and action validation, the repeat reservation (now start_direct_run, agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:1759; for scripts, agents/core/autonomy/jobs_scripts.py:144-146) and the quiet-hours hold on delivery (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:2060; for scripts, agents/core/autonomy/jobs_scripts.py:491-493). - Only the owner's own ▶ now runs a paused job. When ▶ now folds into a queued first run, it makes that request manual (agents/core/autonomy/jobs_dispatch.py:86). - Pausing cancels a not-yet-claimed first run of either origin (cancel_queued, agents/core/autonomy/jobs_dispatch.py:107, called at agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:1695). - An edit that changes what runs (action or options) queues the first run again for the edited job, keeping its origin, instead of letting the claim's identity check drop it (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:1674; _requeue_first_run, agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:1678). A rename or a new schedule leaves it queued. Either way a policy first run meets the policy again at the drain. If the queue refuses the new request, the edit is still saved and says why in the log. If the enqueue is refused at creation (the queue is at capacity, or the database is locked), the answer is still 201 with first_run null and 'first run not queued (…)', because the job is armed and a retry would duplicate it. POST /api/jobs returns the receipt as first_run, or null, plus one confirmation built by arm_confirmation (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:622): - 'first run now, then \<schedule\> (\<cron\>)', or 'first run queued, then …' with a note that nothing fires while the scheduler is not running (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:637); - '\<schedule\> (\<cron\>), on its cadence', with the quiet-hours or near-slot reason when that was the cause. /remind, the CLI and the HUD print it. Tests: - tests/test_job_first_run.py, 74 cases (41 before the second review). 28 of them fail on ccdd7161, with its fixture pointed at that commit's slot helper: - an interval ask job is queued and drained into one run before any slot (tests/test_job_first_run.py:109); - a calendar schedule waits (tests/test_job_first_run.py:123); - the emergency stop (tests/test_job_first_run.py:133); - pause cancels the first run, and one that slips past the pause is still skipped (tests/test_job_first_run.py:143, tests/test_job_first_run.py:155), an asked one too (tests/test_job_first_run.py:451); - ▶ now keeps its force (tests/test_job_first_run.py:164); - edits: one to the action runs the edited job (tests/test_job_first_run.py:176), one the policy would not fire drops it (tests/test_job_first_run.py:387), an asked one survives (tests/test_job_first_run.py:439), a rename leaves it alone (tests/test_job_first_run.py:473), and a refused re-queue still saves (tests/test_job_first_run.py:483); - at the drain: quiet hours that began (tests/test_job_first_run.py:402), a slot now near (tests/test_job_first_run.py:416), and an asked first run that runs anyway (tests/test_job_first_run.py:429); - first_run is a creation choice, never stored (tests/test_job_first_run.py:210); - a refused enqueue and a locked database (tests/test_job_first_run.py:229, tests/test_job_first_run.py:499); - quiet hours, the near slot, a long cadence near its slot and no scheduler (tests/test_job_first_run.py:242, tests/test_job_first_run.py:251, tests/test_job_first_run.py:462, tests/test_job_first_run.py:261); - an interval script job submits its first run (tests/test_job_first_run.py:273); - the interval table, the decision table and the slot timing on the real cron (tests/test_job_first_run.py:306, tests/test_job_first_run.py:339, tests/test_job_first_run.py:520); - both CLI flags (tests/test_job_first_run.py:353, tests/test_job_first_run.py:363). - tests/test_nerva_cli.py:1274 and tests/test_slash_commands.py:373. - frontend/src/test/jobs-first-run.test.ts (armNote). - tests/test_jobs_routes.py: a new reminder still sends nothing until /run, and the script job's /run is again a fresh manual request. Every guard added in the second review was mutated out one at a time, and a test failed each time. 656 job, dispatch, command, CLI and schedule tests pass. One-shot run_at jobs (H450) never take a first run, even when one is asked for: first_run_policy and first_run_decision answer "one-shot" (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:581, :607). The H450 row says they must stay out of the first run. A known pre-existing gap outside this row: parse_schedule drops a window or day qualifier after an interval ("every 30 minutes between 9 and 17" becomes '\*/30 \* \* \* \*'), so such a job runs all day and counts as an interval. Image-recovery collateral review (2026-10-02): changes to shared CLI/image-turn or HUD local-panel disclosure are outside this row's claimed symbols.
